definition.val: Sclerosing cholangitis caused by Cryptosporidium infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Cryptosporidial sclerosing cholangitis and associated biliary complications are characteristic of three primary groups: Hyper-IgM syndromes (both X-linked and autosomal recessive forms), MHC class II deficiency, and DOCK8 deficiency. These conditions typically present with biliary stricturing, jaundice, and progressive hepatic dysfunction due to impaired T-cell mediated clearance of the parasite.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to infection of the lower respiratory tract, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, or lung parenchyma, or by infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

comments: Recurrent lower respiratory tract infections, including bronchiectasis, are characteristic of antibody deficiencies and combined immunodeficiencies.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to Giardia lamblia infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Giardia lamblia, or by Giardia lamblia infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
Increased susceptibility to Giardia lamblia infections as manifested by a chronic or persistent Giardia lamblia infection.

comments: Persistent or chronic Giardia lamblia infections are characteristic of primary immunodeficiencies that impair mucosal antibody production. This phenotype is most frequently associated with X-linked agammaglobulinemia (XLA), Common Variable Immunodeficiency (CVID), and Hyper-IgM syndromes.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to Giardia lamblia infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Giardia lamblia infection.

Increased susceptibility to Toxoplasma gondii infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Toxoplasma gondii, or by Toxoplasma gondii infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

comments: Severe or unusual Toxoplasma gondii infections, including CNS toxoplasmosis, are primarily associated with severe T-cell deficiencies (both primary and secondary). This phenotype has also been specifically described in X-linked Hyper-IgM syndrome, where impaired T-cell signaling increases susceptibility to central nervous system involvement.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to infection involving the heart or major vessels, as manifested by recurrent or severe endocarditis, myocarditis, pericarditis, or infectious vasculitis, or by cardiovascular infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

nodes.lbl: Toxoplasma infection of the central nervous system (CNS)

definition.val: Infection of the central nervous system with Toxoplasma gondii, typically presenting as cerebral toxoplasmosis.
Increased susceptibility to Leishmania infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Leishmania, or by Leishmania infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
Increased susceptibility to Leishmania infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Leishmania.
Increased susceptibility to Leishmania infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Leishmania infection.
Increased susceptibility to parasitic infections that rarely cause disease in immunocompetent individuals.

Increased susceptibility to infectious cholangitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the biliary tract, or by cholangitis occurring in an unusual clinical context such as absence of cholelithiasis or biliary obstruction. Causative agents include bacteria (Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterococcus species) and fungi (Candida species).

Increased susceptibility to infection of the genitourinary tract, as manifested by recurrent or severe cystitis, pyelonephritis, kidney abscess, or vaginal infection, or by genitourinary infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

Increased susceptibility to infection of the eye or its adnexa, as manifested by recurrent or severe conjunctivitis, keratitis, retinitis, or other ocular infection, or by ocular infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

An atypical or infrequent infectious process affecting the liver parenchyma that deviates from common viral or bacterial patterns. This may include infections caused by rare pathogens (e.g., specific fungi, parasites, or rare bacteria) or infections presenting with atypical clinical or pathological features.

comments: This term is intended to capture rare or atypical infectious etiologies of liver inflammation that are not covered by standard viral hepatitis categories (A-E). It includes infections caused by opportunistic pathogens, rare fungi, or parasites in both immunocompetent and immunocompromised hosts.

definition.val: Inflammation of the liver tissue caused by an infectious agent, most commonly viruses (e.g., Hepatitis A, B, C), but also potentially by bacteria, parasites, or fungi. It is characterized by diffuse involvement of the liver parenchyma.

comments: This term refers to diffuse liver inflammation explicitly linked to an infectious agent. While often used interchangeably with viral hepatitis in clinical settings, here it serves as a grouping term for all pathogen-induced diffuse hepatitis, including bacterial and parasitic forms.

definition.val: Sepsis caused by bacterial infection, characterized by a dysregulated host response to a bacterial pathogen with systemic inflammation, organ dysfunction, and potential progression to septic shock.

comments: Causative organisms range from gram-positive cocci such as Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus species to gram-negative bacilli such as Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, and may include anaerobic and atypical bacterial organisms.

definition.val: Sepsis caused by fungal infection, characterized by a dysregulated host response to a fungal pathogen with systemic inflammation, organ dysfunction, and potential progression to septic shock.

comments: Common causative organisms include Candida species (candidaemia), Aspergillus species, Cryptococcus, and the Mucorales, as well as endemic dimorphic fungi.

definition.val: Sepsis or sepsis-like syndrome caused by viral infection, characterized by a dysregulated host response to a viral pathogen with systemic inflammation, multi-organ involvement, and potential progression to circulatory and respiratory failure.

comments: Causative organisms include, among others, influenza virus, SARS-CoV-2, dengue virus, enteroviruses, and various herpesviruses such as cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), and varicella-zoster virus (VZV).

definition.val: Sepsis or sepsis-like systemic illness caused by mycobacterial infection, characterized by a dysregulated host response with systemic inflammation, multi-organ involvement, and disseminated mycobacterial disease.

comments: Causative organisms include Mycobacterium tuberculosis (notably as part of disseminated or miliary tuberculosis) and non-tuberculous mycobacteria.

definition.val: Pneumonia characterized by lobar or segmental consolidation on radiographic imaging, reflecting alveolar filling with inflammatory exudate that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Recurrent pneumonia with consolidation is a characteristic of antibody deficiencies (CVID, X-linked agammaglobulinaemia) and may progress to bronchiectasis if untreated.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to cytomegalovirus (CMV) infections as manifested by severe, invasive, persistent, or disseminated CMV infection.

Increased susceptibility to pleural empyema, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the pleural space, or by empyema occurring in an unusual clinical context such as an atypical causative organism or failure to resolve with standard therapy.
Increased susceptibility to pleural empyema, as manifested by a severe or life-threatening infection of the pleural space requiring surgical drainage, decortication, or intensive care.
Increased susceptibility to pleural empyema, as manifested by recurrent episodes of pleural space infection that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.
Increased susceptibility to infectious endocarditis, as manifested by recurrent or severe endocardial infection, or by endocarditis caused by an unusual organism.
Increased susceptibility to infectious endocarditis, as manifested by severe or complicated endocarditis with valvular destruction, systemic emboli, or heart failure requiring surgical intervention.
Increased susceptibility to infectious endocarditis, as manifested by recurrent episodes of endocardial infection that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.
Increased susceptibility to infectious myocarditis, as manifested by recurrent or severe inflammation of the myocardium caused by infection, or by myocarditis caused by an unusual organism.
Increased susceptibility to infectious myocarditis, as manifested by severe myocardial inflammation with haemodynamic compromise, arrhythmia, or fulminant heart failure.

Increased susceptibility to infectious myocarditis, as manifested by recurrent episodes of myocardial inflammation caused by infection that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.
Increased susceptibility to infectious pericarditis, as manifested by recurrent or severe inflammation of the pericardium caused by infection, or by pericarditis caused by an unusual organism.
Increased susceptibility to infectious pericarditis, as manifested by severe inflammation of the pericardium with pericardial effusion, tamponade, or constrictive pericarditis.

Increased susceptibility to infectious pericarditis, as manifested by recurrent episodes of pericardial inflammation caused by infection that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.

Increased susceptibility to vasculitis caused by infection, as manifested by recurrent or severe vascular inflammation of infectious aetiology, or by infectious vasculitis caused by an unusual organism.
Increased susceptibility to vasculitis caused by infection, as manifested by severe vascular inflammation with ischaemia, infarction, or end-organ damage.

Increased susceptibility to vasculitis caused by infection, as manifested by recurrent episodes of vascular inflammation of infectious etiology that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.
Abscess of the liver caused by bacterial infection. Principal causative agents include Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Bacteroides species, and Staphylococcus aureus.
A liver abscess caused by Staphylococcus aureus infection that may arise from hematogenous spread, biliary infection, or contiguous spread.

synonyms.val: Liver abscess due to Staphylococcus aureus

comments: A recurrent or unusual staphylococcal liver abscess can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection and is a hallmark presentation of chronic granulomatous disease.

definition.val: Abscess of the liver caused by Klebsiella species infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Hepatic abscess due to Klebsiella pneumoniae|Klebsiella pneumoniae liver abscess

definition.val: A liver abscess caused by fungal infection, with common causative organisms including Candida species (often as part of hepatosplenic candidiasis) and Aspergillus species.

comments: A fungal liver abscess most often occurs in the context of severe immunocompromise.

definition.val: Infection of the liver caused by Candida species that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: A characteristic feature of severe T-cell deficiency and neutrophil defects including chronic granulomatous disease.

definition.val: A liver abscess or cystic hepatic lesion caused by parasitic infection, with principal causative organisms being Entamoeba histolytica (amoebic liver abscess) and Echinococcus species (hepatic hydatid disease).

comments: Susceptibility to parasitic liver abscesses (e.g., amebic or hydatid) is primarily determined by environmental exposure and geographic endemicity rather than an underlying immune defect. While severe or atypical cases can occur in immunocompromised states, they are not standard diagnostic markers for primary immunodeficiency.

definition.val: Abscess of the liver caused by Entamoeba histolytica infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

synonyms.val: Liver abscess due to Entamoeba histolytica

definition.val: Cystic or alveolar lesion of the liver caused by Echinococcus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.
Infection of the liver caused by Schistosoma species, occurring in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection, typically presenting with periportal fibrosis or hepatosplenomegaly.

A splenic abscess caused by bacterial infection, typically with organisms such as Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella species, and gram-negative enteric bacteria. It may arise from hematogenous seeding, contiguous spread, or trauma.

comments: A recurrent or unusual bacterial splenic abscess can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in phagocyte defects.

definition.val: A splenic abscess caused by fungal infection, often as part of hepatosplenic candidiasis.

comments: A fungal splenic abscess most often occurs in the context of severe immunocompromise, including neutrophil defects and post-hematopoietic-stem-cell-transplant patients.

definition.val: A splenic abscess or cystic splenic lesion caused by parasitic infection, with causative organisms including Echinococcus species (splenic hydatid disease) and Entamoeba histolytica.

An increased susceptibility to gastroenteritis of infectious etiology, as manifested by a recurrent or severe gastroenteritis, a prolonged diarrhoeal illness, or a gastroenteritis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

synonyms.val: Unusual infectious infection of the gastrointestinal tract

comments: A recurrent or chronic infectious gastroenteritis can be a manifestation of antibody deficiencies or combined immunodeficiencies.

definition.val: A gastroenteritis caused by bacterial infection, with common causative organisms including Salmonella species, Shigella species, Campylobacter, and pathogenic Escherichia coli.

comments: A recurrent or invasive bacterial gastroenteritis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in antibody deficiencies and IL-12/IFN-gamma axis defects.

definition.val: A gastroenteritis caused by viral infection, with common causative organisms including rotavirus, norovirus, adenovirus, astrovirus, and enterovirus.

comments: A chronic or persistent viral gastroenteritis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in antibody deficiencies and severe combined immunodeficiency.

definition.val: A gastroenteritis caused by fungal infection, most often by Candida species. A fungal gastroenteritis can occur in any host with severely disrupted mucosal immunity or following prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotic exposure, and can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.
A gastroenteritis caused by parasitic infection, with causative organisms including Giardia lamblia, Cryptosporidium species, and Microsporidia.

comments: A chronic or recurrent parasitic gastroenteritis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in antibody deficiencies and disorders affecting CD40-CD40L signalling.

definition.val: An increased susceptibility to colitis of infectious etiology, as manifested by a recurrent or severe colonic infection, or by an infectious colitis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

comments: A recurrent or chronic infectious colitis can be a manifestation of antibody deficiencies and combined immunodeficiencies.

definition.val: A colitis caused by bacterial infection, with common causative organisms including Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, enteroinvasive Escherichia coli, and Clostridioides difficile.

comments: A recurrent or severe bacterial colitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

definition.val: A colitis caused by viral infection, with causative organisms including cytomegalovirus, adenovirus, norovirus, and enterovirus.

comments: A viral colitis can occur in immunocompetent hosts but is more common in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in T-cell deficiencies and post-transplant immunosuppression.

definition.val: A colitis caused by fungal infection, most commonly by Candida species.

comments: A fungal colitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in severe T-cell deficiencies, neutrophil defects, or following prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotic exposure.

definition.val: A colitis caused by parasitic infection, with causative organisms including Entamoeba histolytica, Cryptosporidium species, and Strongyloides stercoralis.

comments: A chronic or invasive parasitic colitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

definition.val: An increased susceptibility to pancreatitis of infectious etiology, as manifested by a recurrent or severe infectious pancreatitis, or by a pancreatitis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

comments: An infectious pancreatitis may occur as part of disseminated viral, bacterial, fungal, or parasitic infection.

definition.val: A pancreatitis caused by bacterial infection, which may occur as a complication of bacteraemia, ascending biliary infection, or invasive abdominal infection.

comments: A severe or recurrent bacterial pancreatitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

definition.val: A pancreatitis caused by viral infection, with causative organisms including mumps virus, cytomegalovirus, coxsackievirus, and other enteroviruses.

comments: A viral pancreatitis can occur in any host but can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection in the context of T-cell deficiencies and disseminated viral disease.

definition.val: A pancreatitis caused by fungal infection. Such cases are rare and typically occur as a manifestation of disseminated invasive fungal disease (with Candida or Aspergillus species) in severely immunocompromised hosts.
A pancreatitis caused by parasitic infection, with causative organisms including Cryptosporidium species, Ascaris lumbricoides, and Echinococcus species.

comments: A parasitic pancreatitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in combined immunodeficiencies.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to bacterial cholangitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the biliary tract, or by cholangitis occurring in an unusual clinical context such as absence of cholelithiasis or biliary obstruction. Principal causative agents include Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Enterococcus species.
Increased susceptibility to cystitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the urinary bladder, or by cystitis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

comments: Causative agents include bacteria (Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterococcus species), viruses (adenovirus, BK polyomavirus), and fungi (Candida species).

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to haemorrhagic cystitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe bladder infection with frank haematuria caused by viral or other atypical organisms. Its occurrence is inherently unusual and can indicate significant immune deficiency.

comments: Haemorrhagic cystitis in the context of inborn errors of immunity is predominantly caused by adenovirus and BK polyomavirus, and is a characteristic complication of severe T-cell deficiency and combined immunodeficiency.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to fungal cystitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the urinary bladder caused by fungal organisms.
Increased susceptibility to bacterial cystitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the urinary bladder caused by bacteria, or by bacterial cystitis caused by an atypical organism.

An inflammation of the kidney involving the renal parenchyma, pelvis, and calices, occurring in a manner unusual for a healthy individual of the same age, as manifested by recurrent or severe episodes of pyelonephritis, or by pyelonephritis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism

Abscess of the kidney occurring in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection, as manifested by renal abscess caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism, or by renal abscess occurring in the absence of the usual predisposing factors such as urinary tract obstruction or urolithiasis.
Abscess of the kidney caused by bacterial infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Principal causative agents include Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Proteus mirabilis, and Staphylococcus aureus.

definition.val: Abscess of the kidney caused by fungal infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Principal causative agent is Candida species, typically occurring in the context of T-cell deficiency or neutrophil defects.

definition.val: Abscess of the kidney caused by parasitic infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Principal causative agents include Echinococcus species (renal hydatid cyst) and Entamoeba histolytica.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to vaginal infection, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the vagina or vulvovaginal area caused by bacterial, viral, fungal, or parasitic organisms, or by vaginal infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

Increased susceptibility to bacterial vaginal infection, as manifested by recurrent or severe bacterial vaginosis or vaginal bacterial infection that is unusual in frequency or severity for a healthy individual of the same age.

comments: Common causative agents include Gardnerella vaginalis and vaginal anaerobes including Prevotella species and Mobiluncus species.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to viral vaginal infection, as manifested by recurrent or severe herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection of the vaginal or vulvovaginal area that can occur in the context of immune deficiency.

comments: Severe or disseminated genital HSV infection can be observed in T-cell deficiencies.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to vulvovaginal candidiasis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the vagina or vulvovaginal area caused by Candida species. Predominantly caused by Candida albicans, with Candida glabrata in azole-resistant cases.

comments: Unusual fungal vaginal infection can be observed in individuals with T-cell deficiencies, IL-17 pathway defects, and chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis. Recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis has been documented in patients with IL-12Rbeta1 deficiency and in patients with impaired T-lymphocyte proliferation in response to Candida antigen.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to parasitic vaginal infection, as manifested by recurrent or severe trichomoniasis or other parasitic vaginal infection. A common causative agent is Trichomonas vaginalis, which has been documented in immunocompromised hosts.

An osteomyelitis caused by bacterial infection, with common causative organisms including Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus species, and gram-negative bacilli such as Salmonella and Serratia marcescens.

comments: A recurrent, multifocal, or atypical-organism bacterial osteomyelitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in chronic granulomatous disease, other phagocyte defects, combined immunodeficiencies, STAT3 signaling pathway defects, and asplenia (including sickle cell-related).

definition.val: An osteomyelitis caused by fungal infection, with causative organisms including Candida species, Aspergillus species, and the dimorphic fungi.

comments: A fungal osteomyelitis is most often a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in severe neutrophil defects, chronic granulomatous disease, other phagocyte defects, combined immunodeficiencies, and STAT3 signaling pathway defects.

definition.val: An increased susceptibility to arthritis of infectious etiology, as manifested by a recurrent or severe septic arthritis, or by an infectious arthritis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

comments: A recurrent or polyarticular infectious arthritis can be a manifestation of an inborn error of immunity.

definition.val: An arthritis caused by bacterial infection, with common causative organisms including Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus species, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and Haemophilus influenzae.

comments: A recurrent or polyarticular bacterial arthritis with encapsulated organisms can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in immunodeficiencies.

definition.val: An arthritis caused by fungal infection, with causative organisms including Candida species, Aspergillus species, and Cryptococcus.

comments: A fungal arthritis is most often a manifestation of disseminated fungal disease in severely immunocompromised hosts.

definition.val: An arthritis caused by mycobacterial infection, with causative organisms including Mycobacterium tuberculosis (tuberculous arthritis) and non-tuberculous mycobacteria.

comments: A mycobacterial arthritis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease (MSMD) and combined immunodeficiencies.

definition.val: An increased susceptibility to myositis of infectious aetiology, as manifested by a recurrent or severe inflammation of skeletal muscle caused by infection, or by an infectious myositis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism. Common causative organisms include Staphylococcus aureus (pyomyositis), Streptococcus pyogenes, and Clostridium species (gas gangrene), as well as viral, fungal, and parasitic agents.
A myositis caused by bacterial infection, with common causative organisms including Staphylococcus aureus (pyomyositis) and Streptococcus species.

comments: A recurrent or invasive bacterial myositis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

definition.val: A myositis caused by fungal infection, with causative organisms including Candida species, Aspergillus species, and the Mucorales. A fungal myositis is rare and typically a manifestation of severe immunocompromise.
A myositis caused by mycobacterial infection, with causative organisms including Mycobacterium tuberculosis and non-tuberculous mycobacteria.

comments: A mycobacterial myositis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease (MSMD) and combined immunodeficiencies.

definition.val: A myositis caused by viral infection, with causative organisms including enterovirus, influenza virus, coxsackievirus, and HIV.

comments: A chronic enteroviral myositis (often presenting as a dermatomyositis-like syndrome) can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in X-linked agammaglobulinaemia.

definition.val: A meningitis caused by viral infection, with common causative organisms including herpes simplex virus, varicella-zoster virus, enterovirus, and CMV. A recurrent or chronic viral meningitis (particularly chronic enteroviral meningoencephalitis) can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

A meningitis caused by bacterial infection, with common causative organisms including Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and Haemophilus influenzae type b. A recurrent or invasive bacterial meningitis with encapsulated organisms can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in antibody deficiencies, complement deficiencies, and asplenia.

A meningitis caused by parasitic infection, with causative organisms including Toxoplasma gondii, Acanthamoeba, and Naegleria fowleri. A parasitic meningitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

A meningitis caused by mycobacterial infection, with the principal causative organism being Mycobacterium tuberculosis (tuberculous meningitis). A non-tuberculous mycobacterial meningitis is rare and can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease.

An encephalitis caused by fungal infection, with causative organisms including Cryptococcus neoformans, Aspergillus species, Candida species, and the Mucorales. A fungal encephalitis is most often a manifestation of disseminated invasive fungal disease in severely immunocompromised hosts.

An encephalitis caused by parasitic infection, with causative organisms including Toxoplasma gondii (toxoplasmic encephalitis), Acanthamoeba, and Naegleria fowleri. A parasitic encephalitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

An encephalitis caused by mycobacterial infection, with the principal causative organism being Mycobacterium tuberculosis (tuberculous encephalitis, often as part of CNS tuberculosis). A mycobacterial encephalitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease.

A brain abscess caused by bacterial infection, with causative organisms including Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus species, anaerobes, and gram-negative bacilli. It may arise from contiguous spread (sinusitis, otitis) or hematogenous seeding, and a bacterial brain abscess can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in phagocyte defects.

A brain abscess caused by fungal infection, with causative organisms including Aspergillus species, Cryptococcus, Candida, and the Mucorales. A fungal brain abscess is most often a manifestation of disseminated invasive fungal disease in severely immunocompromised hosts.

A brain abscess caused by parasitic infection, with causative organisms including Toxoplasma gondii, Entamoeba histolytica, and Echinococcus species. A parasitic brain abscess can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

A brain abscess caused by mycobacterial infection, with the classic manifestation being a tuberculoma caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. A mycobacterial brain abscess can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease.

Increased susceptibility to infection of the spinal cord, as manifested by infectious myelitis, spinal epidural or intradural abscess, or spinal cord compression due to infectious spondylodiscitis occuring in an unusual clinical context such as an atypical causative organism, absence of the usual predisposing factors, or by occurrence in the context of immune deficiency. Principal causative agents include bacteria (Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, Mycobacterium tuberculosis), fungi (Aspergillus species, Candida species), and viruses (enteroviruses, VZV, CMV).

An increased susceptibility to bacterial infection of the skin, as manifested by a recurrent or severe cutaneous bacterial infection, or by a skin infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism. Common causative organisms include Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus species. A recurrent bacterial skin infection can be a manifestation of phagocyte defects, hyper-IgE syndrome, and atopic dermatitis-related immune defects.

Increased susceptibility to bacterial skin abscesses, as manifested by recurrent, multifocal, or unusually severe collections of pus within the dermis or deeper skin layers. While common causative organisms include Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus species, this term also encompasses abscesses caused by opportunistic or atypical bacteria, or those that are refractory to standard antibiotic therapy.

A recurrent infection of hair follicles producing furuncles (boils), with common causative organisms being Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus species. A recurrent boil can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in chronic granulomatous disease, hyper-IgE syndrome (STAT3 deficiency), leukocyte adhesion deficiency, and atopic dermatitis-related immune defects.
A cellulitis caused by bacterial infection of the dermis and subcutaneous tissue, with common causative organisms including Streptococcus pyogenes and Staphylococcus aureus.

comments: A recurrent or severe bacterial cellulitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, including phagocyte defects, lymphoedema-associated immune defects, and complement deficiencies.

definition.val: An increased susceptibility to viral infection of the skin, as manifested by a recurrent or severe cutaneous viral infection, or by a skin infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism. Common causative organisms include herpes simplex virus, varicella-zoster virus, human papillomavirus, and Molluscum contagiosum.

comments: A recurrent or disseminated viral skin infection can be a manifestation of T-cell deficiencies, DOCK8 deficiency, and WHIM syndrome.

definition.val: A herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection of the skin, which may present as localised vesicular lesions in any host. A severe, persistent, or disseminated cutaneous HSV infection (including eczema herpeticum and chronic ulcerative herpes) can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

An increased susceptibility to parasitic infection of the skin or subcutaneous tissue, as manifested by a recurrent, severe, or atypically distributed parasitic skin lesion, or by a cutaneous parasitic infection occurring in an unusual clinical context. Causative organisms include Leishmania species, Onchocerca volvulus, and Ancylostoma species. An atypical or disseminated cutaneous leishmaniasis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.
Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) skin infection including chickenpox or herpes zoster that is unusually severe or persistent.

An increased susceptibility to fungal infection of the skin or subcutaneous tissue, as manifested by a recurrent, severe, or atypically distributed fungal lesion, or by an infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism. Common manifestations include chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis or subcutaneous mycoses (such as sporotrichosis caused by Sporothrix species.

comments: An unusual fungal skin infection is a hallmark of T-cell deficiencies, inborn errors of IL-17 immunity (e.g., STAT1 gain-of-function, AIRE deficiency), and CARD9 deficiency, which specifically predisposes to deep dermatophytosis and subcutaneous fungal invasion.

definition.val: Recurrent nappy (diaper) rash of infectious aetiology, typically caused by Candida.

Increased susceptibility to infection of the nail apparatus, including the nail plate, nail bed, nail matrix, and proximal nail fold, as manifested by recurrent or severe nail infection, or by nail infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

comments: Causative agents include bacteria (Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus species) causing paronychia, and fungi (dermatophytes, Candida species) causing onychomycosis.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to bacterial infection of the nail bed and proximal nail fold (paronychia), as manifested by recurrent or severe episodes that are unusual in frequency or severity for a healthy individual of the same age. Principal causative agents include Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus species.

comments: Recurrent bacterial paronychia is a characteristic feature of phagocyte defects including leukocyte adhesion deficiency and chronic granulomatous disease.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to herpes simplex virus (HSV) infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with HSV, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

Increased susceptibility to recurrent fungal nail infection (onychomycosis), as manifested by recurrent or persistent infection of the nail plate, nail bed, or nail matrix caused by dermatophytes (Trichophyton species) or Candida species.

comments: Recurrent onychomycosis is a characteristic feature of chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis (CMC) due to STAT1 gain-of-function, STAT3 loss-of-function, or other IL-17 pathway defects.

definition.val: An increased susceptibility to mycobacterial infection of the skin, as manifested by persistent, disseminated, or multifocal cutaneous lesions occurring in an unusual clinical context. This includes skin involvement in tuberculosis (Mycobacterium tuberculosis) or infections caused by atypical mycobacteria (nontuberculous mycobacteria), such as M. marinum, M. avium complex, or M. chelonae.

comments: Unusual mycobacterial skin infections are highly characteristic of Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease (MSMD), affecting the IL-12/IFN-gamma axis, as well as GATA2 deficiency and other profound T-cell deficiencies.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to infection of the fascia and surrounding soft tissue, as manifested by necrotizing fasciitis or other invasive fascial infection occurring in an unusual clinical context. Necrotizing fasciitis is a rapidly progressive, life-threatening infection of the superficial fascia and subcutaneous tissue.

comments: Principal causative agents include Streptococcus pyogenes (type I, monomicrobial) and polymicrobial infections involving anaerobes, Gram-negative organisms, and Staphylococcus aureus (type II). Immunocompromise is present in approximately 50% of cases.

definition.val: Infestation of the skin by migrating hookworm larvae (principally Ancylostoma braziliense and Ancylostoma caninum), causing serpiginous, pruritic, erythematous cutaneous tracks. Although typically self-limited in immunocompetent hosts, cutaneous larva migrans may follow a prolonged or atypical course in the context of immune deficiency, including HIV/AIDS and other T-cell defects.

Infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissue by Leishmania species, as manifested by cutaneous or mucocutaneous leishmaniasis occurring in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection. Cutaneous leishmaniasis presents with chronic, non-healing ulcerative skin lesions.

synonyms.val: Unusual susceptibility to cutaneous Leishmania infection

comments: In the context of inborn errors of immunity, susceptibility to Leishmania species is associated with defects in the IL-12/IFN-gamma axis, including Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease (MSMD) gene defects.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to gingivitis, as manifested by severe or necrotising gingival infection, including necrotising ulcerative gingivitis, associated with significant tissue destruction.
Increased susceptibility to periodontitis, as manifested by recurrent or chronic periodontal infection that is unusual in frequency or severity for a healthy individual of the same age
Increased susceptibility to dental abscess, as manifested by a severe or invasive dental abscess with systemic spread or requiring hospitalisation.
Increased susceptibility to dental abscess, as manifested by recurrent episodes of dental abscesses that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.

Increased susceptibility to infectious stomatitis, as manifested by severe or invasive oral mucosal infection causing necrosis or aphthous ulceration of tissue, or requiring systemic antiviral or antimicrobial therapy.
Increased susceptibility to infectious stomatitis, as manifested by recurrent episodes of oral mucosal infection that are unusual in frequency or severity for a healthy individual of the same age.

Increased susceptibility to oral candidiasis caused by Candida albicans, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the oral mucosa, or by oral thrush occurring beyond the neonatal period without an identifiable predisposing cause.
Increased susceptibility to oral candidiasis, as manifested by severe or invasive oropharyngeal infection with Candida albicans, including extension to the oesophagus or systemic spread.

Increased susceptibility to pharyngitis, as manifested by a severe episode of pharyngeal infection requiring hospitalisation or intravenous antimicrobial therapy, or complicated by peritonsillar abscess, retropharyngeal abscess, or invasive spread.

comments: Principal causative agents include Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A Streptococcus) and Fusobacterium necrophorum.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to otitis media, as manifested by a severe episode of middle ear infection requiring hospitalisation, intravenous antibiotics, or surgical intervention, or complicated by mastoiditis, meningitis, or other invasive spread.

Increased susceptibility to otitis externa, as manifested by a severe or invasive infection of the external ear canal, including necrotising (malignant) otitis externa with involvement of surrounding bone or soft tissue.

Increased susceptibility to otitis externa, as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection of the external ear canal that are unusual in frequency or severity for a healthy individual of the same age.
Increased susceptibility to infectious conjunctivitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the conjunctiva, or by conjunctivitis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

comments: Principal causative agents in the context of immune deficiency include adenovirus (epidemic keratoconjunctivitis, which may follow a prolonged or severe course in immunocompromised hosts), herpes simplex virus, and enterovirus.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to infectious conjunctivitis, as manifested by a severe episode with corneal involvement (keratoconjunctivitis), subepithelial infiltrates, or requiring systemic antiviral or antimicrobial therapy.
Increased susceptibility to infectious conjunctivitis, as manifested by recurrent episodes of conjunctival infection that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.
Increased susceptibility to infectious keratitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the cornea, or by keratitis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

comments: Principal causative agents in the context of immune deficiency include herpes simplex virus (HSV stromal keratitis, with a recurrence rate of 50% in immunodeficient patients) and varicella-zoster virus (herpes zoster ophthalmicus with corneal involvement). Immunodeficiency is a significant independent risk factor for recurrent HSV keratitis.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to infectious keratitis, as manifested by a severe episode of corneal infection with stromal involvement, corneal ulceration, perforation, or significant visual impairment.
Increased susceptibility to infectious keratitis, as manifested by recurrent episodes of corneal infection that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.

comments: Recurrent HSV keratitis is a hallmark of T-cell immunodeficiency and is associated with progressive corneal scarring and visual loss.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to infectious retinitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the retina, or by retinitis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

comments: The principal causative agent in the context of immune deficiency is cytomegalovirus (CMV retinitis), which is a hallmark of severe T-cell deficiency and combined immunodeficiency. Other agents include VZV (acute retinal necrosis) and HSV.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to infectious retinitis, as manifested by severe or extensive retinal infection with rapid progression, retinal detachment, or significant visual loss.
Increased susceptibility to infectious retinitis, as manifested by recurrent episodes of retinal infection that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.
A family history (in a first- or second-degree relative) of unusually severe, recurrent, or opportunistic infection.
A family history (in a first- or second-degree relative) of an immune deficiency.

synonyms.val: Familiy history of primary immunodeficiency disorders (PID)
Family history of an inborn error of imunity (IEI)

definition.val: A family history (in a first- or second-degree relative) of an autoimmune disease.

nodes.lbl: Family history of death due to infection

definition.val: A family history of death of a first- or second-degree relative caused by infection.
A family history (in a first- or second-degree relative) of a lymphoma.

comments: A family history of lymphoma may indicate inherited cancer predisposition syndromes, including DNA repair defects, and inborn errors of immunity predisposing to lymphoproliferative disease such as X-linked lymphoproliferative syndrome and ITK deficiency.

definition.val: A family history (in a first- or second-degree relative) of a leukaemia.

comments: A family history of leukaemia may indicate inherited bone marrow failure syndromes, DNA repair defects, or inborn errors of immunity predisposing to malignancy, including GATA2 deficiency, SAMD9/SAMD9L disorders, and Fanconi anaemia.

definition.val: A maternal history of recurrent miscarriage, defined as two or more pregnancy losses.

synonyms.val: Maternal history of recurrent spontaneous abortion

definition.val: Death of a sibling that remains unexplained despite investigation, which may indicate an undiagnosed disease in the family.

A reproductive relationship between two individuals who are related by blood as second cousins or closer. In a medical and genetic context, consanguinity increases the coefficient of inbreeding, raising the probability that an offspring will inherit identical alleles from a common ancestor (homozygosity by descent). This significantly increases the risk for autosomal recessive disorders, such as inborn errors of immunity, metabolic diseases, and rare neurodevelopmental syndromes. A history of consanguinity serves as a vital clinical marker for directing diagnostic investigations toward recessive genetic etiologies, especially in the presence of rare phenotypes or unexplained family medical history.

An osteomyelitis caused by mycobacterial infection, with causative organisms including Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Mycobacterium bovis BCG (typically as a complication of BCG vaccination), and non-tuberculous mycobacteria.

comments: A mycobacterial osteomyelitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease (MSMD) and combined immunodeficiency.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to infection of bones, joints, or muscles, as manifested by recurrent or severe osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, or infectious myositis, or by musculoskeletal infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

comments: Recurrent musculoskeletal infections are characteristic of phagocyte defects, sickle cell-related asplenia, and combined immunodeficiencies.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to osteomyelitis of infectious aetiology, as manifested by recurrent or severe bone infection, multifocal osteomyelitis, or osteomyelitis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

comments: Recurrent or multifocal osteomyelitis is a characteristic manifestation of various diseases, such as chronic granulomatous disease, phagocyte defects, innate signaling defects (such as MyD88 or IRAK4 deficiency), IFN-gamma pathway defects, and humoral immunodeficiencies (such as XLA).

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to infection involving lymph nodes or lymphatic vessels, as manifested by recurrent or severe lymphadenitis or lymph node abscess, or by lymphatic infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.
Infection of the oral cavity including the gingiva, periodontium, teeth, tongue, or oral mucosa that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.
Infection with attenuated mumps vaccine virus following mumps vaccination, occurring in the context of unusual susceptibility to live viral vaccines.
Retinitis caused by cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: CMV retinitis is an atypical manifestation of cytomegalovirus, most commonly encountered as an opportunistic infection in immunocompromised hosts.

definition.val: Pneumonitis caused by cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: CMV pneumonitis is an atypical manifestation of cytomegalovirus, most commonly encountered as an opportunistic infection in immunocompromised hosts.

definition.val: Encephalitis caused by cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: CMV encephalitis is an atypical manifestation of cytomegalovirus, most commonly encountered as an opportunistic infection in immunocompromised hosts.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infections as manifested by severe or disseminated disease or impaired control of EBV infection.
Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) triggered by Epstein-Barr virus infection.
Disseminated infection with herpes simplex virus (HSV), involving multiple organ systems.
Increased susceptibility to herpes simplex virus (HSV) infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of HSV infection.
Persistent or recurrent detection of adenovirus in the blood that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Persistent adenoviral viraemia is characteristic of T-cell deficiencies, severe combined immunodeficiency, and post-transplant immunosuppression, and may progress to disseminated adenoviral disease.

definition.val: Colitis caused by adenovirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Adenoviral colitis is an opportunistic gastrointestinal manifestation characteristic of T-cell deficiencies and immunocompromised hosts, presenting with prolonged or severe diarrhoea, dehydration, and intestinal mucosal injury.

definition.val: Hepatitis caused by adenovirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Adenoviral hepatitis is an opportunistic manifestation seen in T-cell deficiencies and post-transplant patients, and may present with elevated transaminases, coagulopathy, or fulminant hepatic failure.

definition.val: Encephalitis caused by adenovirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Adenoviral encephalitis is a rare but severe opportunistic manifestation typically seen in severe T-cell deficiencies and immunocompromised hosts, presenting with seizures, focal neurological deficits, or altered consciousness.

definition.val: Pneumonitis caused by adenovirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Adenoviral pneumonitis is an opportunistic manifestation characteristic of T-cell deficiencies and stem cell transplant recipients, often presenting with severe hypoxia, diffuse pulmonary infiltrates, and respiratory failure.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to varicella (chickenpox) infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of chickenpox infection.
Increased susceptibility to varicella (chickenpox) infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with varicella (chickenpox).
Encephalitis caused by varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: VZV encephalitis is an opportunistic CNS manifestation characteristic of T-cell deficiencies and may also occur as a complication of severe primary varicella or zoster reactivation, presenting with altered consciousness, seizures, or focal neurological deficits.

definition.val: Pneumonitis caused by varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: VZV pneumonitis is a severe complication of primary varicella or disseminated zoster, characteristic of T-cell deficiencies and immunosuppressed hosts, and may present with hypoxia, diffuse pulmonary nodular infiltrates, and respiratory failure.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to human papillomavirus (HPV) causing warts infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with HPV causing warts, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
Increased susceptibility to human papillomavirus (HPV) manifested by unusually severe, extensive, or invasive warts.
Increased susceptibility to human papillomavirus (HPV), manifested by recurrent episodes of warts.

Increased susceptibility to chronic or persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection causing warts that fail to clear over an extended period or recur after treatment that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Chronic warts are characteristic of T-cell deficiencies (DOCK8, GATA2), WHIM syndrome (CXCR4), and epidermodysplasia verruciformis (EVER1, EVER2, CIB1).

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to Molluscum contagiosum infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Molluscum contagiosum infection.
Increased susceptibility to norovirus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with norovirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

Increased susceptibility to chronic or persistent norovirus infection, as manifested by prolonged viral shedding and recurrent or unremitting gastrointestinal symptoms beyond the typical course of acute infection.

comments: Chronic norovirus infection is characteristic of antibody deficiencies (CVID, X-linked agammaglobulinaemia) and combined immunodeficiencies, and may cause persistent diarrhoea, malabsorption, and failure to thrive.

definition.val: Hepatitis caused by Aichi virus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Aichi virus hepatitis has been described as a rare opportunistic manifestation in patients with primary antibody deficiencies and severe combined immunodeficiency, and represents a clinically distinct gastrointestinal/hepatic viral infection in IEI.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to enterovirus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with enterovirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
Infection of the central nervous system by enterovirus that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Enteroviral CNS infection, including chronic enteroviral meningoencephalitis, is a hallmark of X-linked agammaglobulinaemia and other antibody deficiencies, and may present with progressive neurological deterioration, dermatomyositis-like syndrome, or fatal meningoencephalitis.

definition.val: Sepsis or sepsis-like syndrome caused by enterovirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Enteroviral sepsis is a severe systemic manifestation typically seen in neonates, patients with antibody deficiencies, or immunocompromised hosts, presenting with multi-organ involvement, haemodynamic instability, and high mortality.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to astrovirus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with astrovirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
Disseminated infection with astrovirus involving organs beyond the gastrointestinal tract that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Disseminated astrovirus infection is a rare opportunistic manifestation described primarily in severe combined immunodeficiency and post-transplant patients, and may present with viraemia, encephalitis, or multi-organ involvement.

definition.val: Infection of the central nervous system by astrovirus that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Astroviral CNS infection, typically presenting as encephalitis or meningoencephalitis, has been described as a rare but recognised manifestation in patients with severe combined immunodeficiency and primary antibody deficiencies.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to influenza virus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with influenza virus.
Persistent or recurrent detection of influenza virus in the blood or prolonged shedding in respiratory secretions that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

comments: Persistent influenza infection is characteristic of T-cell deficiencies and immunocompromised hosts, and may be associated with prolonged respiratory illness, antiviral resistance, and severe lower respiratory tract complications.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to parainfluenza virus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with parainfluenza virus.
Increased susceptibility to parainfluenza virus infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of parainfluenza virus infection.

A persistent SARS-CoV-2 infection with prolonged active viral replication and continuous detection of virus beyond the typical duration of acute COVID-19, typically lasting several weeks or longer, often with culturable virus and intra-host viral evolution. A chronic COVID-19 infection is distinct from post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (long COVID), which represents a post-infectious syndrome after viral clearance, and from recurrent COVID-19 reinfections, which are common in the general population.

comments: A chronic COVID-19 infection can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in B-cell-depleted patients (following rituximab, anti-CD20 therapy, CAR-T cell therapy, or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation), antibody deficiencies, and combined immunodeficiencies.

definition.val: A severe infection caused by a seasonal coronavirus (HCoV-229E, HCoV-OC43, HCoV-NL63, or HCoV-HKU1), characterized by lower respiratory tract involvement, hypoxia, or systemic illness beyond that typically seen with these viruses in immunocompetent hosts.

comments: A severe seasonal coronavirus infection can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in T-cell deficiencies and post-hematopoietic-stem-cell-transplant patients.

definition.val: A persistent infection with a seasonal coronavirus (HCoV-229E, HCoV-OC43, HCoV-NL63, or HCoV-HKU1) with prolonged active viral replication beyond the typical duration of acute infection.

comments: A chronic seasonal coronavirus infection can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in antibody deficiencies and combined immunodeficiencies.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with HHV-6, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location, such as the brain.
Increased susceptibility to human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with HHV-8, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

comments: Unusual or severe HHV-8 infections, including Kaposi sarcoma, are primarily associated with severe T-cell deficiencies (both primary and secondary) and CD4 T-cell lymphopenia. This phenotype has also been specifically described in cases of Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome.

definition.val: Nephropathy caused by BK polyomavirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

synonyms.val: Nephropathy caused by a Human polyomavirus 1 infection

comments: BK virus nephropathy is an opportunistic manifestation characteristic of solid organ transplant recipients (particularly renal transplant) and hematopoietic stem cell transplant patients, presenting with progressive renal dysfunction and tubulointerstitial nephritis.

definition.val: Encephalitis caused by BK polyomavirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

synonyms.val: Encephalitis caused by a Human polyomavirus 1 infection

comments: BK virus encephalitis is a rare opportunistic CNS manifestation typically seen in severe T-cell deficiencies and post-transplant patients. It may also present as Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), involving either BK or JC polyomavirus, and has been specifically described in cases of Hyper-IgM syndrome and DOCK8 deficiency. Clinical presentations often include altered consciousness, seizures, or focal neurological deficits.

definition.val: Increased susceptibility to JC polyomavirus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with JC polyomavirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
Nephropathy caused by JC polyomavirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

synonyms.val: Nephropathy caused by a Human polyomavirus 2 infection

comments: JC virus nephropathy is a rare opportunistic manifestation described in T-cell deficiencies and post-transplant patients, presenting with progressive renal dysfunction and tubulointerstitial inflammation.

definition.val: Encephalitis caused by JC polyomavirus infection, typically presenting as progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML).

synonyms.val: Encephalitis caused by a Human polyomavirus 2 infection

comments: JC virus encephalitis is an opportunistic CNS infection typically seen in severe T-cell deficiencies and post-transplant patients. It often presents as Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) and has been specifically described in DOCK8 deficiency and Hyper-IgM syndrome. Clinical manifestations typically include progressive neurological deficits, cognitive impairment, and ataxia.

definition.val: Granulomatous inflammation with multiple granuloma formation attributable to a causative infectious agent, including bacteria, mycobacteria, fungi, or parasites.

Granulomatous inflammation involving the formation of multiple granulomas not attributable to a causative infectious agent, arising in the context of immune dysregulation, foreign-body reactions or idiopathic.
Granulomatous inflammation characterized by the formation of multiple granulomas exhibiting caseation necrosis, in which the necrotic tissue acquires an amorphous, cheese-like appearance.
Granulomatous inflammation characterized by the formation of multiple granulomas without central caseation necrosis.

An interstitial lung disease, characterized by lymphocytic infiltration and/or granulomatous inflammation of the lung after exclusion of infection and alternative causes, often associated with multisystem inflammatory or granulomatous disease in patients with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID).
Lymph node enlargement resulting from granulomatous inflammation, characterized by compact aggregates of epithelioid macrophages and giant cells within the lymph node parenchyma.
A non-infectious inflammatory granulomatous dermatosis characterized by annular or disseminated erythematous plaques resulting from palisading granulomas with central mucin deposition in the dermis.
Inflammation of the synovial membrane characterized by granuloma formation within synovial tissue, consisting of aggregates of epithelioid histiocytes with or without multinucleated giant cells.

Uveitis characterized by granulomatous inflammatory pattern of the uveal tract, with clinical findings that may include large keratic precipitates, iris nodules, or other signs of intraocular granulomatous inflammation.
Inflammation of the gingiva characterized by granulomatous tissue reaction, with compact aggregates of epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleate giant cells within the gingival lamina propria.
Inflammation of the iris characterized by granulomatous tissue reaction, with compact aggregates of mononuclear phagocytes within the iris stroma.

An increased susceptibility to Burkholderia pseudomallei infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Burkholderia pseudomallei, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

An increased susceptibility to coagulase-negative staphylococci infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with coagulase-negative staphylococci, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An increased susceptibility to coagulase-negative staphylococci infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of coagulase-negative staphylococci infection.
An increased susceptibility to coagulase-negative staphylococci infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with coagulase-negative staphylococci.
An increased susceptibility to Enterococcus faecalis infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Enterococcus faecalis, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An increased susceptibility to Enterococcus faecalis infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.
An increased susceptibility to Enterococcus faecalis infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Enterococcus faecalis.
An increased susceptibility to Enterococcus faecium infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Enterococcus faecium, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An increased susceptibility to Enterococcus faecium infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.
An increased susceptibility to Enterococcus faecium infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Enterococcus faecium.

An increased susceptibility to viridans group streptococci infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with viridans group streptococci, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

nodes.lbl: Endocarditis caused by Streptococcus viridans infection

definition.val: An endocarditis caused by infection with viridans group streptococci, which are a characteristic causative agent of subacute bacterial endocarditis.

synonyms.val: Subacute bacterial endocarditis due to viridans streptococci

nodes.lbl: Liver abscess due to Streptococcus viridans

definition.val: A liver abscess caused by infection with viridans group streptococci, which may arise from hematogenous spread, biliary infection, or contiguous spread.

synonyms.val: Hepatic abscess due to Streptococcus viridans

definition.val: An increased susceptibility to Mycobacterium abscessus infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Mycobacterium abscessus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An increased susceptibility to Mycobacterium abscessus infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.
An increased susceptibility to Mycobacterium abscessus infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Mycobacterium abscessus.

An increased susceptibility to Mycobacterium avium complex infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Mycobacterium avium complex, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

synonyms.val: Unusual susceptibility to Mycobacterium avium complex

definition.val: An increased susceptibility to Mycobacterium avium complex infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.
An increased susceptibility to Mycobacterium avium complex infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Mycobacterium avium complex.
An increased susceptibility to Mycoplasma infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Mycoplasma, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An increased susceptibility to Mycoplasma infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.
An increased susceptibility to Mycoplasma infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Mycoplasma.
An increased susceptibility to Ureaplasma infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Ureaplasma, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An infection of the lungs caused by Cryptococcus species, which is the most common entry portal for cryptococcal disease and may present as nodules, consolidation, or interstitial infiltrates.

comments: A pulmonary cryptococcosis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in severe T-cell deficiencies, idiopathic CD4 lymphopenia, and anti-GM-CSF autoantibody syndromes.

definition.val: A granulomatous mass-like lesion caused by Cryptococcus infection, which may occur in the lung, brain, skin, or other organs.

comments: A cryptococcoma can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in T-cell deficiencies and immunosuppressed hosts.

definition.val: An increased susceptibility to Mucorales infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Mucorales, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An increased susceptibility to Talaromyces marneffei infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Talaromyces marneffei, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An increased susceptibility to dermatophytes infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with dermatophytes, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An increased susceptibility to dermatophytes infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.

nodes.lbl: Increased CD4+ TEMRA T cell proportion

definition.val: An abnormally increased proportion of CD4-positive TEMRA T cells (terminally differentiated effector memory T cells re-expressing CD45RA), relative to total CD4-positive T cells in the blood. These cells have a CD45RA-positive, CD45RO-negative, CCR7-negative phenotype.

An increased susceptibility to mould infection, as manifested by a recurrent or severe invasive infection with filamentous fungi other than Aspergillus, or by a mould infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism. Common causative organisms include Fusarium species, Scedosporium species, and Lomentospora prolificans.

comments: An invasive mould infection most often occurs in the context of severe immunocompromise, particularly in prolonged neutropenia and post-hematopoietic-stem-cell-transplant patients.

definition.val: An increased susceptibility to Blastomyces dermatitidis infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Blastomyces dermatitidis, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An increased susceptibility to Blastomyces dermatitidis infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.
An increased susceptibility to Blastomyces dermatitidis infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Blastomyces dermatitidis.
An increased susceptibility to Coccidioides infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Coccidioides, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An increased susceptibility to Coccidioides infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.
An increased susceptibility to Coccidioides infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Coccidioides.

An increased susceptibility to Paracoccidioides brasiliensis infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Paracoccidioides brasiliensis, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An increased susceptibility to Paracoccidioides brasiliensis infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.
An increased susceptibility to Paracoccidioides brasiliensis infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Paracoccidioides brasiliensis.
An increased susceptibility to Histoplasma capsulatum infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.
An increased susceptibility to Candida auris infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Candida auris, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An increased susceptibility to chronic or persistent Candida auris infection, as manifested by prolonged infection with this multi-drug-resistant emerging Candida species.
An increased susceptibility to Candida auris infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Candida auris.
A hepatitis caused by herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection, which may present as a severe or fulminant hepatitis with elevated transaminases, coagulopathy, and hepatic failure.

comments: An HSV hepatitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in T-cell deficiencies, neonates, and immunosuppressed hosts.

definition.val: A meningitis caused by varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infection, which may occur as part of primary varicella, herpes zoster, or zoster sine herpete (without rash).

comments: A VZV meningitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in T-cell deficiencies and immunosuppressed hosts.

definition.val: A molluscum contagiosum lesion exceeding one centimetre in diameter, which may present as an unusually large, persistent, or atypical lesion.

comments: A giant molluscum can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in DOCK8 deficiency, GATA2 deficiency, and severe T-cell deficiencies.

definition.val: An increased susceptibility to human herpesvirus 7 (HHV-7) infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with HHV-7, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
A cystitis caused by BK polyomavirus infection, typically presenting as haemorrhagic cystitis with macroscopic haematuria.

comments: A BK cystitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients and severely immunocompromised hosts.

definition.val: An increased susceptibility to poliovirus infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with poliovirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

A chronic shedding of poliovirus in stool over an extended period, typically following vaccination with live attenuated oral poliovirus vaccine, with viral excretion persisting for months or years. A chronic poliovirus excretion is characteristic of antibody deficiencies including X-linked agammaglobulinaemia and common variable immunodeficiency, in which patients may shed vaccine-derived poliovirus indefinitely.
An increased susceptibility to rotavirus infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with rotavirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An increased susceptibility to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with RSV, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

synonyms.val: Unusual susceptibility to respiratory syncytial virus

definition.val: An increased susceptibility to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).

An increased susceptibility to chronic or persistent respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, as manifested by prolonged viral shedding and persistent or recurrent respiratory symptoms beyond the typical course of acute infection.
An increased susceptibility to rhinovirus infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with rhinovirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An increased susceptibility to human metapneumovirus (hMPV) infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with hMPV, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.
An ocular infection caused by Toxoplasma gondii, typically presenting as chorioretinitis with characteristic retinal lesions and potential progression to vision loss.

comments: A Toxoplasma eye infection can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in T-cell deficiencies and congenital toxoplasmosis.

definition.val: An adverse disease following vaccination with the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) live attenuated Mycobacterium bovis vaccine, ranging from local BCGitis (regional lymphadenitis or injection-site abscess) to disseminated BCGosis. BCG associated disease can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in severe combined immunodeficiency, Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease (MSMD), and chronic granulomatous disease.

nodes.lbl: Abnormal effector memory CD4+ T cell proportion

definition.val: An abnormal proportion of effector memory CD4-positive memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These are memory cells that are short-lived cells that migrate to the site of an infection and attempt to eliminate the pathogen. These cells may have a CD3/CD4/CD62L-/CD45RA phenotype.

nodes.lbl: Abnormal central memory CD4+ T cell proportion

definition.val: An abnormal proportion of central memory CD4-positive memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CCR7-positive, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Abnormal decrease of absolute number (either count per volume or proportion of total lymphocytes) of T cells or of a subset of T cells, commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These may include both TCR alpha/beta and gamma/delta T cells.

synonyms.val: Decreased numbers of circulating T cells

definition.val: Abnormal increase of absolute number (either count per volume or proportion of total lymphocytes) of T cells or of a subset of T cells, commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These may include both TCR alpha/beta and gamma/delta T cells.

Abnormal decrease in the proportion of T cells, commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, measured as a percentage of total lymphocytes in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These may include both TCR alpha/beta and gamma/delta T cells.

Abnormal increase in the proportion of T cells, commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, measured as a percentage of total lymphocytes in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These may include both TCR alpha/beta and gamma/delta T cells.

nodes.lbl: Decreased total CD4+ T cell number

definition.val: Abnormal decrease of absolute number of helper CD3+CD4+ T cells (either count per volume or percentage of total lymphocytes), compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

Abnormal increase of absolute number of helper CD3+CD4+ T cells (either count per volume or percentage of total lymphocytes), compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

nodes.lbl: Increased total CD4+ T cell count
