definition.val: Abnormal increase of absolute count of helper CD3+CD4+ T cells (quantified as count per volume), compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

synonyms.val: Increased circulating CD4+ T cell count

nodes.lbl: Decreased total CD4+ T cell count

definition.val: Abnormal decrease of absolute count of helper CD3+CD4+ T cells (quantified as count per volume), compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

synonyms.val: Decreased circulating CD4+ T cell count

definition.val: A reduction in one or more peripheral blood cell lineages resulting from immune-mediated destruction or impairment caused by an autoimmune process.
A severe form of eczema characterised by extensive skin involvement and/or persistent or recurrent symptoms requiring intensive treatment.
A chronic inflammatory liver disease characterised by immune-mediated hepatocellular injury resulting from an autoimmune process.

A disorder of the brain not caused by an infectious agent, characterised by inflammation of the brain parenchyma. It may present with an altered level of consciousness, focal or multifocal neurologic deficits, and seizures; unlike infectious encephalitis, fever is often absent, and autoimmune forms frequently present subacutely with cognitive, psychiatric, or behavioural changes.
An inflammation of the brain parenchyma caused by an autoimmune process directed against neuronal or glial antigens.

nodes.lbl: Increased total CD8+ T cell number

definition.val: Abnormal increase of the absolute number of cytotoxic CD3+CD8+ T cells (measured the absolute count per volume or as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood), compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

nodes.lbl: Decreased total CD8+ T cell number

definition.val: Abnormal decrease of the absolute number of cytotoxic CD3+CD8+ T cells (measured the absolute count per volume or as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood), compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

nodes.lbl: Decreased total CD8+ T cell count

definition.val: Abnormal decrease of cytotoxic CD3+CD8+ T cells, measured as the total count per volumne in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

synonyms.val: Decreased circulating CD8+ T cell count

nodes.lbl: Increased total CD8+ T cell count

definition.val: Abnormal increase of cytotoxic CD3+CD8+ T cells, measured as the total count per volumne in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.
Infection of the lung parenchyma with herpes simplex virus, resulting in inflammation of the lung parenchyma with impaired respiratory function.

synonyms.val: Pneumonia due to herpes simplex virus

definition.val: Recurrent episodes of conjunctivitis caused by infection with Haemophilus influenzae, characterised by inflammation of the conjunctiva associated with conjunctival injection and purulent ocular discharge.

comments: Recurrent or severe Haemophilus influenzae infections are commonly reported in patients with primary antibody deficiencies and may represent an important clue to an underlying defect in humoral immunity.

definition.val: A structural deformity of the hindfoot, the posterior region of the foot formed by the talus and calcaneus.
A tendency to mix up left and right in one's own body space, typically elicited by asking a person to perform a two-stage command involving specified lateralized anatomy.

comments: Some suggest that a tendency to mix up left and right of an examiner's body space is a more reliable feature sensitive.

definition.val: The concentration of DNAJB9 in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

synonyms.val: DNAJB9 protein level in serum elevated
Elevated DnaJ homolog subfamily B member 9 concentration
Elevated DnaJ homolog subfamily B member 9 level
Elevated DnaJ homolog subfamily B member 9 level in blood
Increased DnaJ homolog subfamily B member 9 concentration
Increased DnaJ homolog subfamily B member 9 level
Increased DnaJ homolog subfamily B member 9 level in blood

comments: DNAJB9 is a proteomic tissue biomarker for fibrillary glomerulonephritis.

definition.val: A partial or complete break in the olecranon,which is the proximal articular portion of the ulna and makes up part of the elbow.

comments: The olecranon is the proximal articular portion of the ulna. Along with the coronoid process, it forms the greater sigmoid (semilunar) notch which articulates with the humerus to provide flexion and extension of the elbow.

definition.val: Past medical history of surgical breast removal.
A malignant neoplasm arising from the endothelial cells of the lymphatic vessels.
Aspiration or inhalation of lipid-containing products.

comments: Exogenous lipoid pneumonia is caused by aspiration or inhalation of lipid-containing products. In the past, the most common agents included mineral oil-based laxatives and nasal decongestants. Other causes include inhalation of petroleum jelly used as a lubricant, e.g., tracheostomy care. The incidence of exogenous lipoid pneumonia is growing exponentially in all age groups secondary to the phenomenon termed vaping. In the latter case, consider the term Electronic cigarette exposure histor (HP:0430032).

definition.val: Symmetric poikiloderma of hips and lateral thighs below the greater trochanter.

comments: The Holster sign may indicate dermatomyositis.

definition.val: A rare neoplasm consisting of a monomorphic population of basaloid epithelial cells, and it accounts for approximately 1-2% of all salivary gland tumors.

comments: Thee most frequent location of basal cell adenoma (BCA) of the salivary gland is the parotid gland. It usually appears as a firm and mobile slow-growing mass. Histologically, isomorphic cells in nests and interlaced trabecules with a prominent basal membrane are observed. In contrast to pleomorphic adenoma, it tends to be multiple and its recurrence rate after surgical excision is high.

definition.val: Elevated Hemidiaphragm is a condition where one portion of the diaphragm is higher than the other. Elevated hemidiaphragm occurs when one side of the diaphragm becomes weak from muscular disease or loss of innervation due to phrenic nerve injury.

The cerebriform connective tissue nevus (CCTN) is one of the most characteristic skin findings. It commonly occurs on the soles of the feet, and frequently causes problems because of pain, pruritus, infection, bleeding,exudation, odor, and walking impairment.

comments: The cerebriform connective tissue nevus is frequently observed in patients with Proteus syndrome and it is an important specific criterion for diagnosis.

definition.val: Linear streaks and swirls of macular hyperpigmentation along the lines of Blaschko.

comments: Blaschko's lines are attributed to the migration lines of epidermal cells during embryogenesis and are characterized by a V-shaped pattern on the posterior midline, S-shape on the abdomen, and spiral on the posterior scalp.

definition.val: The experience of remorse, self-reproach, or perceived culpability for a real or perceived unfavorable outcome. Guilt may be proportionate to the context or disproportionate, and it may occur in the absence of an identifiable act, event, or offense. It reflects the interplay of cognitive processes, such as judgments about responsibility, and emotional responses, which can lead to persistent rumination or preoccupation. Guilt may extend to situations outside the individual's control and, in some cases, be accompanied by inaccurate or exaggerated beliefs about one's role in an outcome.

comments: The individuals frequently feel they have violated their own, or universal, moral standards. Guilt often reflects a relationship between disordered thinking or cognitive processes (such as cognitive distortions) and emotional dysregulation resulting in persistent ruminations or preoccupations of remorse and shame. In severe cases, guilt may be associated with delusional beliefs, as seen in psychotic depression.

definition.val: A deviation of the mediastinum from its normal position in the midline of the thoracic cavity. The mediastinum is a compartment of the thoracic cavity that contains the heart and its blood vessels, the esophagus, trachea, thymus, as well as nerves and lymph nodes.

comments: Since the pleural cavity is confined by the rib cage, large pleural effusion may push the structures in the thoracic cavity to the opposite side resulting in a shift of the upper and lower mediastinum. Other etiologies are also observed. See Figures 1 and 2 of PMID:35990927 or Figure 1 of PMID:37680422.

definition.val: Dyspnea as a result of bending forward while not holding one's breath; dyspnea or shortness of breath onset within 30 seconds of bending forward.

comments: Bendopnea is mediated by increased ventricular filling pressure during bending, which exacerbates an already high filling pressure in patients with heart failure.

definition.val: Refers to pain that is worse when the affected individual lies down (flat).
Abnormally increased ability to move of the tympanic membrane.

comments: In Stickler syndrome, hypermobility is sometimes associated with thin, visibly hyperflaccid tympanic membranes, which is a common and otoscopically detectable sequela of chronic or recurrent otitis media and/or previous tympanostomy tubes. Hypermobility may also be found with normal appearance tympanic membranes.

definition.val: Concentration of vitamin B12 in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

comments: Elevated levels of serum cobalamin may be a sign of a serious, even life-threatening, disease. Hematologic disorders like chronic myelogeneous leukemia, promyelocytic leukemia, polycythemia vera and also the hypereosinophilic syndrome can result in elevated levels of cobalamin.

definition.val: The concentration of sFASL (soluble FASL, soluble FAS-ligand) in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

comments: The first apoptosis signal receptor (FAS) pathway regulates apoptosis and is critical for proper development and functioning of the immune system. FAS ligand (FASL) can bind to FAS receptors.

definition.val: A disorder of the internal anal sphincter (IAS) in which the IAS fails to relax that manifests clinically as intractable constipation.

comments: The internal anal sphincter, which is a specialized smooth muscle continuation of the circular muscle layer of rectum, plays a significant role in the maintenance of anorectal continence and in the pathophysiology of incontinence and constipation. Internal anal sphincter achalasia is a clinical condition with presentation similar to Hirschsprung disease but with the presence of ganglion cells on suction rectal biopsy.

definition.val: History of treatment with an anthracycline chemotherapy agent.
A pattern of episodic heavy alcohol use characterized by the consumption of a high number of drinks per occasion.

comments: The World Health Organization defines binge drinking (BD) based on a cut-off of six drinks (i.e., 60g of alcohol) or more per occasion. The National Institute on Alcoholism and Alcohol Abuse (NIAAA) defines BD as a pattern of drinking that brings blood alcohol concentration (BAC) levels to 0.08 g/dL, which typically occurs after 4 drinks (i.e., 56 g of alcohol) for women and 5 drinks (i.e., 70 g of alcohol) for men in about 2 hours.

definition.val: Concentration of thrombopoietin in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal. Thrombopoietin is a glycoprotein hormone produced by the liver and kidney that stimulates the production and differentiation of megakaryocytes.

A rare hamartomatous malformation characterized by the predominant proliferation of normal collagen fibers and normal, decreased, or increased elastic fibers. Collagenomas may be solitary or multiple, sporadic, acquired or inherited.

nodes.lbl: Lack of sufficient daily physical activity

definition.val: Physical activity levels less than those required for optimal health and prevention of premature death.

A phenomenon whereby stimulation of one sensory or cognitive pathway leads to automatic, involuntary experiences in a second sensory or cognitive pathway. For instance, people with synaesthesia may experience unusual colors, tastes, and other sensations when engaged in everyday activities like reading or listening to music.
Abnormally dark color of cerumen (earwax), which is a waxy substance secreted in the ear canal that normally has a brown, orange, red, yellowish or gray.
A history of high intake of spciy foods with ingrediaents such as capsaicin, pepper, chili, ginger, garlic, onion, fenugreek, and turmeric.

nodes.lbl: Oil-drop brown pigmentation of the corneal limbus

definition.val: Brown pigment spots in the limbus (border between the cornea and the sclera).

Hazardous drinking is defined as a quantity or pattern of alcohol consumption that places individuals at risk for adverse health events. This could include alcohol use despite potentially hazardous or risky consequences, such as operating heavy machinery or drunk driving.
Excessive fear of embarrassment, humiliation, or rejection when exposed to possible negative evaluation by others when engaged in a public performance or social interaction.
Flat affect and reduced response to emotional stimuli. Fear and anger responses that are normally present are blunted.

Phaeohyphomycosis refers to infections due to a large group of heterogenous organisms called dematiaceous or melanized fungi. These fungi are distinguished by the predominance of melanin in their cell walls, which likely acts as a virulence factor. Virtually, everyone is exposed to dematiaceous fungi through inhalation, as they are ubiquitous in the environment, although the development of infection is extremely uncommon.

comments: Invasive disease is rare but remains important due to the ability to cause serious disease in immunocompetent and immunocompromised hosts, unlike other fungal infections such as aspergillosis.

definition.val: Hearing one's own voice resonating loudly in the ear.
A history of being at high altitude in situations such hiking, mountain climbing, travel to mountains, or air travel.
A past medical history of recently being hospitalized.

comments: This may imply a nosocomial infection risk.

definition.val: Cessation of palpitations can be induced by Valsava maneuver.

comments: In patients who can terminate their palpitations with a Valsalva maneuver, this is thought to indicate possibly a supraventricular tachycardia.

definition.val: Abnormally long telomeres in somatic cells.

nodes.lbl: Reduced circulating aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase activity

definition.val: The activity of aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (also known as DOPA decarboxylase, tryptophan decarboxylase, and 5-hydroxytryptophan decarboxylase) in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
Abnormal narrowing of the subclavian artery.
Cardiac synchronous pulsation on palpation.

comments: A pulsating liver is characteristic of significant tricuspid regurgitation. Systolic pulsations of the liver in patients with primary severe tricuspid regurgitation are due to transmission of a prominent right atrial v wave.

definition.val: Neuropathic pain is triggered by lesions to the somatosensory nervous system that alter its structure and function so that pain occurs spontaneously and responses to noxious and innocuous stimuli are pathologically amplified.

comments: Neuropathic pain can be characterized by pain that is triggered when clothes touch the skin, spontaneous burning that feels like boiling water, bursts of pins and needles(paresthesias) in the feet upon walking , a continuous crushing pain after an amputation as if your phantom foot is being squeezed, or a band of searing pain around the body at the level at whichsensation was lost after a spinal cord injury.

definition.val: A history of repeated exposure to cold water, as may result, for instance, from surfing, diving, kayaking, or swimming.
Tinnitus (sound heard by a subjhect when no corresponding external sound is present) that is made worse by swallowing.

comments: During swallowing, the tensor veli palatini (TVP) muscle is activated to assist in elevating the palate. Due to this dual innervation by CNV, the tensor tympani (TT) muscle can be activated and possibly cause tinnitus in some patients.

nodes.lbl: Rhythmic movements of the tympanic membrane

definition.val: Regularly occurring motion of the tympanic membrane (eardrum), which is located between the inner and middle ear. This can be a manifestation of tensor tympani myoclonus, which can also be ascertained as sawtooth patterns on long-term tympanometry.

The length of the temporal styloid process is above the upper limit of normal. The styloid process is a cylindrical, slender, needle-like projection of varying lengths averaging 2 to 3 cm. The styloid process projects from the inferior part of the petrous temporal bone and offers attachment to the stylohyoid ligament and the stylohyoid, stylopharyngeus, and styloglossus muscles.
Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with nitroglycerin.
Pulsus paradoxus refers to a systolic pressure drop greater than 10mmHg during inspiration.

comments: Pulsus paradoxus results from alterations in the mechanical forces imposed on the chambers of the heart and pulmonary vasculature and is often due to pericardial disease, particularly cardiac tamponade and to a lesser degree constrictive pericarditis.

definition.val: Chest pain can be induced by palpation of the chest, which may be an indication of costochondritis.
Discomfort in the chest described as pressure, heaviness, or tightness.

nodes.lbl: Chest pain described as ripping or tearing

definition.val: Chest pain described as a tearing or ripping sensation.

comments: The pain of aortic dissection may be described as tearing or ripping and does not improve with nitroglycerin.

definition.val: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by bending (flexing) a joint.
Applies to a finding that is situated or occurring around the thorax (chest).
Applies to a finding that is situated or occurring in or on the penis.

nodes.lbl: Snowstorm pattern of uterus on ultrasound

definition.val: A sonographic snowstorm pattern of the uterus that results from the presence of a complex vesicular intrauterine mass containing many grape-like cysts.

comments: The snowstorm sign is the classic appearance of a complete hydatiform mole. The sign results from multiple hydropic villi and has the ultrasonographic appearance of a central heterogeneous mass with a solid, hyperechoic area together with numerous cystic areas and filling the entire uterine cavity.

definition.val: History of multiple previous births.
History of exposure to aquatic animals.

comments: Mycobacterium marinum is an opportunistic pathogen inducing infection in fresh and marine water fish. Human infections with Mycobacterium marinum have been associated with the exposure of damaged skin to polluted water from fish pools or contacting objects contaminated with infected fish. Fish mycobacteriosis is clinically manifested and characterized in man by purple painless nodules, liable to develop into superficial crusting ulceration with scar formation.

definition.val: Multiple, oblong, fatty lesions in the superficial subcutaneous fatty tissue. They are mostly under 2 cm in long axis diameter. They demonstrate nodular (blush-like) increased fluid signal at unenhanced MRI and are markedly hyperechoic at ultrasound.

comments: These lesions are characteristicv of Adiposis dolorosa (Dercum's disease).

definition.val: Presence of giant cells in the dermis. Giant cells are formed by fusion of various cells such as macrophage, epithelioid cells, monocytes, etc., These are multi-nucleated, large in size, and generally present at the site of chronic inflammation and other granulomatous conditions.

nodes.lbl: Exacerbation of eyelid lesion by crying

definition.val: Applies to an eyelid lesion such as hemangiomas or varices that swells upon crying.
Applies to an abnormality that is situated in the upper eyelid.
Repetitive air swallowing and belching and that may result in abdominal distention.

nodes.lbl: Vaginal passage of hydatidiform mole tissue

definition.val: Passage from the vagina of hyatidiform tissue, appearing as clusters of vesicles (similar to small grapes) developed from the transformation of chorionic villi. This is a manifestation of a molar pregnancy (hyatidiform mole).

synonyms.val: Solid tissue passed by the vagina

definition.val: Abnormal fluid that seeps out of the nipple of the breast. Nipple discharge is categozied as lactational, physiologic, or pathologic.
The presence of gallstones within the intrahepatic bile ducts proximal to the right and left hepatic ducts.

comments: Hepatolithiasis is benign in nature, but the prognosis is poor due to an association with recurrent cholangitis, biliary strictures, liver abscesses, and atrophy or cirrhosis of the affected liver. Hepatolithiasis is also a known risk factor for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.

definition.val: Abnormally frequent belching (expelling gas noisily from the stomach through the mouth).

Fibrosis located in the subepithelial portion of the esophagus. Fibrosisis is defined by the overgrowth, hardening, and/or scarring of various tissues and is attributed to excess deposition of extracellular matrix components including collagen.
This term refers to pain that is triggered by extending (straightening) the leg.

comments: This feature may suggest spinal problems such as spinal epidural abscess.

definition.val: Amount of pyrophosphate uptake by the myocardium as demonstrated by by technetium pyrophosphate (99mTc-PYP) scintigraphy above the upper limit of normal.
Refers to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by anesthetic block of a nerve.
Tear film break up time (number of seconds that elapse between the last blink and the appearance of the first dry spot in the tear film) below the lower limit of normal.

A granuloma localized to the skin, that is, a chronic inflammatory manifestation with localized aggregation of histiocytes with or without other inflammatory cells (such as plasma cells, eosinophils, or neutrophils), with or without necrosis, with or without vasculitis, with or without calcification, and with or without foreign bodies. Granulomas may be due to infection or chronic inflammatory disease or reactions to foreign material.
Formation of abnormal, extraskeletal bony tissue in the dermis (i.e., the layer of skin that lies beneath the epidermis and above the subcutaneous layer).

nodes.lbl: Thinning of outer muscular layer of small bowel

definition.val: The depth of the outer muscular layer of the small bowel is below the lower limit of normal.

A developmental anomaly of renal lymphatics that results from a failure of the lymphatics to make communication with the rest of the lymph trunks. The abnormal lymphatics thus dilate and form cystic spaces at the renal sinus and in the perinephric space.
A myxoma (benign, locally infiltrative neoplasms arising from mesenchymal origin) localized to the pharynx.
Fibrin thrombi inside subcutaneous arterioles.

Vasculitis (inflammation of blood vessels) in the kidney. Renal vasculitis can be observed with numerous disorders and presents clinically as rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN) which is characterized by acute kidney injury (AKI), haematuria and proteinuria. Histological examination of the kidney reveals severe inflammation in the form of crescent formation, glomerular necrosis and vasculitis of small and medium sized vessels within the kidney.

nodes.lbl: Pancreatic islet beta cell iron deposition

definition.val: Accumulation of abnormally high amounts of iron in beta cells of the pancreas.
A hamartoma (tissue malformation consisting of an abnormal mixture of constitutive components) originating in the nose.

A type of metachromasia localized to a peripheral nerve. Metachromasia may be defined as the staining of tissue or tissue components such that the color of the tissue-bound dye complex differs significantly from the color of the original dye complex to give a marked contrast in color. For instance in metachromatic leukodystrophy, bloated Schwann cells, containing granularmetachromatic storage material May display a characteristic yellow green dichroism under crossed polarised light.

comments: In metachromatic leukodystrophy, galactosyl sulfatide (cerebroside sulfate) accumulates in the white matter of the CNS and in the peripheral nerves. Galactosyl sulfatide, and to a lesser extent lactosyl sulfatide, also accumulate within the kidney, gallbladder, and certain other visceral organs and are excreted in excessive amounts in the urine. In histologic preparations, they form spherical granular masses that stain metachromatically (i.e., with a color different from that of the dye solution). See Figure 2 of PMID:16291896.

nodes.lbl: Reduced phosphoserine phosphatase activity in cultured fibroblasts

definition.val: Activity of phosphoserine phosphatase below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

nodes.lbl: Reduced alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase activity in cultured fibroblasts

definition.val: Activity of alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

synonyms.val: Alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase low in fibroblasts

definition.val: Activity of beta-ureidopropionase in the liver below the lower limit of normal.
Activity of dihydropyrimidinase in the liver below the lower limit of normal.
Fontanelle that is more deeply set than normal. Fontanelles are normally relatively firm and curve only slightly inward. A sunken fontanelle can be a sign of dehydration or marasmus.
Formation of an angle (tilt) along the shaft of the penis.

comments: This finding can be observed with penis fracture and Peyronie Disease. The latter is caused by a plaque (scar tissue) that pulls on the surrounding tissues and causes the penis to curve or bend, usually during an erection.

nodes.lbl: History of urethral procedure or catheterization

definition.val: A past medical history of a procedure or catheterization involving the urethra.
Abormal enlargement of the penis owing to accumulation of fluid.
Activity of the enzyme alpha-1,4-glucosidase activity in muscle tissue is below the lower limit of normal.

A brown tumor is a bone lesion that results from bony resorption by excess osteoclastic activity, and replacement by fibrous tissue and giant cells. Brown tumor is an uncommon pathognomonic sign of hyperparathyroidism.

Flame-figures are composed of a central part consisting of collagen fibers and eosinophilic granules, surrounded by a histiocytic and eosinophilic infiltrate. Subsequently, eosinophils tend to disappear and are replaced by phagocytic granulomas, consisting of histiocytes and sometimes giant cells, around the flame figures.

comments: Flame figures may be observed in Wells syndrome.

definition.val: Applied to a sign or symptom that is present during pregnancy and becomes worse following birth.
History of having taken retinoids.
History of having been treated with propylthiouracil.

History of spending a substantial amount of time outdoors with occupation or hobbies related to the outdoors, including hunting, gardening, farming, agriculture, horticulture, miners, working in wet fields.
A sinus tract is an abnormal channel that originates from the skin or a mucous surface to a deep-seated focus of suppuration.

synonyms.val: Tract under skin draining associated abscess

comments: A soft tissue ulcer can show a sinus tract leading to a deeper soft tissue abscess and may occasionally extend to a joint. Chronic osteomyelitis can be associated with a sinus tract and cloaca (opening or rupture of bony cortex overlying an area of osteomyelitis) draining granulation tissue, pus, or necrotic debris from the bone to the skin.

definition.val: Past medical history of surgical replacement of the cornea with corneal tissue from a donor.
Breakage of the capsule of the lens. This is most often observed as a complication of lens surgery, but this term refers to lens capsule rupture not related to surgery or major trauma.

comments: Spontaneous lens capsule rupture has been observed with Marshall syndrome.

definition.val: A past medical history of wearing contact lenses.
Increase in thickness of the mucosa of the airways above the upper limit of normal.

comments: This feature can be observed in mucolipidosis type II. Progressive airway thickening can lead to respiratory insufficiency.

definition.val: Increased (more negative) voltage across the nasal epithelium.

comments: The resulting (or basal) potential difference (PD) is negative or polarized (viewed from the epithelial surface) and in normal subjects, it is usually between -15 and -25 mV. The measurement continues by the sequential perfusion of compounds that block inwardly directed sodium transport through inhibition of ENaC (amiloride), followed by augmentation of chloride transport through CFTR. During perfusion of amiloride, the potential difference depolarizes as ENaC transport is reduced, and the PD typically approaches a low polarizing value (typically between 0 and -10 mV).

definition.val: An adhesion between the conjunctiva of the eyelid and the cornea.

Intraductal papilloma is a benign tumor found within breast ducts. The abnormal proliferation of ductal epithelial cells causes growth. A solitary intraductal papilloma is usually found centrally posterior to the nipple affecting the central duct. Multiple intraductal papillomas are located peripherally, found in any breast quadrant affecting the peripheral ducts.
Precipitous labor is extremely rapid labor and delivery, usually defined as expulsion of the fetus within less than 3 hours of commencement of regular contractions.
Maternal history of a pregnancy with two fetuses in the uterus.
A swelling or enlargement localized to the vagina. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.
Pain that is elicited by palpation of the region inside of the costovertebral angle, which is formed by the 12th rib and the spine.

comments: Costovertebral angle tenderness can be observed with conditions including pyelonephritis and ureteral stones.

definition.val: Pain that is elicited by moving the uterine cervix. This finding can be ascertained by pelvic exam. Cervical motion tenderness is a gynecological exam finding that could be indicative of peritoneal infection.
Fluid that originates from the urethra that is not urine, pre-ejaculate or semen.
The presence of an extra digital crease in and individual with normal joint anatomy.
Refers to a phenotypic abnormality that mainly affect large joints.
Refers to a phenotypic abnormality that affects a single joint.
An abnormality of the upper palmar crease whereby the crease widens and ends between the second and third fingers and is said to resemble a hockey stick.

comments: See figure 5 of PMID:29094891.

definition.val: The amount of succinyladenosine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
The amount of 5-hydroxymethyluracil in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
The amount of creatinine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is below the lower limit of normal.
The amount of deoxyuridine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
The amount of dihydrouracil in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
The amount of dihydrothymine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

The amount of sulfatides in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal. Sulfatides are derived from GalCer via esterification of a sulfate group to 3-hydroxyl of the galactose moiety.
The amount of xanthurenic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
Presence of N-acetylglucosamine-rich oligosaccharides in the urine.
The amount of 2'-deoxyadenosine (dAdo) in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
Positive (abnormal) result of the 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine urine test, which indicates the presence of alpha-ketoacids in the urine.
The amount of dolichol in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
The amount of bile acids in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is below the lower limit of normal.
The ratio of creatine to creatinine concentration in the urine is above the upper limit of normal.

comments: This finding is suggestive of a disorder of creatine metabolism.

definition.val: The amount of thymidine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
The amount of glutarylglycine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is below the lower limit of normal.

Detection of indican in the urine. Urinary indican concentration may be elevated in small bowel bacterial overgrowth. Indican is produced by bacterial deconjugation of dietary tryptophan to indole which is absorbed at all levels of the intestine, but principally from the small bowel.
Dacryolith is a concretion (accumulation of sediment) within the nasolacrimal system.

comments: Dacryoliths may cause intermittent epiphora without inflammation, or recurrent dacryocystitis may develop.

nodes.lbl: Reduced erythrocyte gamma-glutamyl cysteine synthetase activity

definition.val: Activity of gamma-glutamylcysteine synthetase (EC 6.3.2.2) in erythrocytes below the lower limit of normal.

synonyms.val: Gamma-glutamyl cysteine synthetase low in erythrocytes

nodes.lbl: Decreased erythrocyte nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide-cytochrome b5 reductase activity

definition.val: The activity of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH)-cytochrome b5 reductase in erythrocytes (red blood cells) is below the lower limit of normal.

nodes.lbl: Reduced alpha-methylacyl-CoA racemase activity in cultured fibroblasts

definition.val: Activity of alpha-methylacyl-CoA racemase (AMACR; EC 5.1.99.4) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

Volume of semen in ejaculate below the lower limit of normal. This finding can be ascertained by semen analysis. Comment: Sperm are produced within the testis, in the process of spermatogenesis, then travel through the male reproductive tract (the seminiferous tubules, epididymis, vas deferens, prostate and urethra). As the sperm travel, seminal fluid is added from the seminal vesicles, prostate, testis and epididymis and periurethral glands. The function of the ejaculate is to transport sperm into the female genital tract and to provide a suitable environment for sperm survival during this transit.
Applies to an abnormality that is situated in (or predominant in) the elbow.
Abnormal enlargement of the visible portion of the distal nail matrix that extends beyond the proximal nail fold, which is referred to as the lunula.
Applies to an abnormality that is situated in (or predominant in) the heel.
Thin, red to reddish-brown lines of blood (hemorrhages) under the nails. Splinter hemorrhages run vertically under the nails.

comments: Splinter hemorrhages represent rupture of longitudinally oriented nail plate capillaries leading to extravasation and the historical hallmark of linear discoloration. See figure 1 of PMID:36050132.

definition.val: Lateral thrust (LT) refers to an abnormal knee joint motion in the early stance phase where the knee joint center moves laterally. Also known as varus thrust, LR is defined as the dynamic worsening or abrupt onset of varus (bow-leg) alignment as the limb accepts weight (stance phase), with a return to less varus and more neutral alignment during lift-off and the non-weight-bearing (swing) phase of gait, varus thrust is a potent mechanical risk factor for medial knee osteoarthritis progression.

comments: LT visualized during walking is associated with a greater medial knee load and an increased risk of medial knee osteoarthritis (OA) progression.

definition.val: A contusion is a region of injured tissue in which blood capillaries have been ruptured without laceration (bruise). Brain contusions are bruises of the cortical surface that damage the surface from the outside inward, producing disruption of tissue and vessels. The term cerebral contusion describes the pathology of focal necrosis and hemorrhage, typically observed in older children, involving particularly cerebral cortex and subcortical white matter. Such lesions are usually found in coup and contrecoup, as well as inferior orbital, frontal, and temporal locations. Cerebral contusions cause permanent damage to tissues of the cerebrum. The etiology of cerebral contusion is trauma to the head.

comments: Cerebral contusion is the classic example of focal traumatic brain injury (TBI). In the pre-CT era, cerebral contusion could be diagnosed only in the operating room during craniotomy or at the autopsy table. Initially, the CT may show isodense or hypodense areas, sometimes mixed-density lesions commonly surrounded by perilesional hypodense areas, but later more surrounding edema with progression over time. Multiple focal contusions may have a salt and pepper appearance. The bone window is used for the evaluation of skull fractures. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is not indicated in the acute management of TBI. If acutely done, there are isointense to hyperintense areas on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images. Fluid-attenuated inversion recovery images demonstrate petechial hemorrhages that are isointense to the brain. The MRI can show ischemic areas and changes from diffuse axonal injury. It can be used later for cognitive problems.

definition.val: A mass of accumulated hardened fecal matter.
Appendicitis is an inflammation of the vermiform appendix, which is a hollow organ located at the tip of the cecum, usually in the right lower quadrant of the abdomen.
A severely scarred portion of infarcted ventricular myocardium that does not contract normally but instead bulges outward while the rest of the ventricle contracts during systole.

comments: A left ventricular aneurysm is one of the worst complications after acute myocardial infarction. The natural course leading to the formation of a ventricular aneurysm involves a full-thickness infarct that has been replaced by fibrous tissue. This inert portion cannot take part in the contraction and herniates outward during systole. Most of the LV aneurysms are asymptomatic and are found in follow-up echocardiography. However, large symptomatic LV aneurysms can cause heart failure, ventricular tachyarrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death.

definition.val: An abnormal form of the heart seen upon chest radiography in which the heart displays an upturned apex and slight concave pulmonary artery segment. This configuration is said to resemble a boot.
Hydrosalpinx is a distension or dilatation of the fallopian tube in the presence of a distal tubal occlusion.

comments: The most common cause of hydrosalpinx is pelvic inflammatory disease.

definition.val: An increase in the level of 3-methylhex-2,4-dienedioic acid or 3-methylhex-3,4-dienedioic acid in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
Increased signal (contrast enhancement) surrounding the liver observed on computer tomography or magnetic resonance imaging following administration of contrast agents.

comments: See figure 2 of PMID:35528764.

nodes.lbl: Reduced in vitro contracture test threshold

definition.val: The in vitro contracture test determines the sensitivity of freshly obtained skeletal muscle specimens to caffeine or halothane applied to a bathing solution. Muscles from persons susceptible to malignant hyperthermia have lower contracture thresholds for these agents than do normal muscle.

synonyms.val: Caffeine in vitro contracture test positive
Halothane in vitro contracture test positive

definition.val: Reduced strength (amplitude) of the F-wave, which is an electrophysiological artifact produced by antidromic activation of motoneurons following distal electrical stimulation of motor nerve fibers.

comments: Because F-waves traverse the entire length of a peripheral nerve between the spinal cord and muscle, F-waves provide a means of examining transmission between stimulation sites in the arm and the leg and the related motoneurons in the cervical and lumbosacral cord. The F-wave is so named because it was originally studied in the small muscles of the foot. It is one of several responses that may follow the direct motor (M) response evoked by electrical stimulation of mixed or motor nerves.

definition.val: Abnormal increase in size of peroxisomes.

comments: See figure 2 of PMID:2894756.

definition.val: A non-malignant growth, or enlargement, of the adrenal glands, specifically the cortex, although the cortex cannot be definitively identified by conventional imaging. Adrenal cortical hyperplasia is defined radiologically as a non-malignant growth, or enlargement, of the adrenal glands.

comments: Controlled by the pituitary gland, the adrenal cortex drives critical processes, such as the production of cortisol, mineralocorticoid and sex hormones. Any disruption in the multiple enzymes and hormones involved in these pathways may cause serious or life-threatening symptoms, often associated with anatomical changes in the adrenal glands.

nodes.lbl: Lymphocytic infiltration of the parotid gland

definition.val: Accumulation of lymphocytes in the parotid gland. This feature is generally defined as a count of lymphocytes per area that is above normal limits on histopathological examination.

A granuloma (a focal aggregate of immune cells that forms in response to a persistent inflammatory stimulus) localiyed to the bone marrow. A granuloma characteristically demonstrates the compact organization of mature macrophages, which may or may not be associated with other inflammatory cell types.
The presence of intracellular inclusion bodies (aggregates of stainable substances, usually proteins) in neurons.
Wasting (shrinking) of the pancreas.

comments: Pancreatic atrophy is commonly seen in elderly patients and may also be a sequela of conditions including chronic pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, and Shwachman-Bodian-Diamond syndrome.

definition.val: Number (count) of pancreatic acinar cells reduced below normal. This feature can be ascertained by pancreas biopsy.

nodes.lbl: Unesterified cholesterol accumulation in cultured fibroblasts

definition.val: An abnormal result of the filipin test. This test is based on the reaction of unesterified cholesterol with fluorescent antibiotic filipin giving a strongly fluorescent, stable cholesterol-filipin complex suitable for in situ detection. An abnormal test result is present if there is a perinuclear accumulation of staining in lysosomal storage organelles (LSOs).

comments: The filipin test is useful for the evaluation of impaired cholesterol esterification in cultured cells (fibroblasts or others) in Niemann-Pick disease type C.

definition.val: Accumulation of foamy cells (lipid-laden macrophages) in the parenchyma of the spleen.
Concentration or activity of N-acetylglutamate synthase in liver tissue below the lower limit of normal.
Ingestion of large amounts of licorice.

comments: Licorice is a popular sweetener found in many soft drinks, food products, snacks and herbal medicines. Licorice toxicity is characterized by the symptom triad of hypertension, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis, so-called pseudohyperaldosteronism. The active ingredient in licorice is glycyrrhizin, which is converted to 3beta-monoglucuronyl-18beta-glycyrrhetinic acid (3MGA) and 18beta-glycyrrhetinic acid (GA) in the gut. These active metabolites inhibit the 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type II enzyme and prevent the conversion of cortisol to cortisone. Unlike cortisone, cortisol binds to the mineralocorticoid receptor. This cortisol excess leads to increased potassium and proton excretion as well as to sodium and water retention, with increased systemic resistance. The triad of symptoms typical of classic hyperaldosteronism (Conn syndrome) results from the aldosterone-like effect: hypokalemia, hypertension, and metabolic alkalosis.

definition.val: Applies to an abnormality that is situated in (or predominant in) the shoulder.

Intrauterine devices (IUDs) are used for contraception. Rarely pregnancy occurs despite the presence of an IUD. Such pregnancies are associated with an increased risk of spontaneous abortion and preterm delivery due to infection, and a higher risk of maternal septic complications.
The mother of a fetus or index patient has a history of folate deficiency during the corresponding pregnancy.
The mother of a fetus or index patient has a history of abnormally low zinc levels during the corresponding pregnancy.

comments: Maternal zinc deficiency may increase the risk low birth weight (LBW) and small for gestational age (SGA) infants.

definition.val: Intrauterine devices (IUD) are commonly used for contraception. IUD complications are rare, but include perforation, pelvic infection, expulsion, missing strings, and difficult IUD removal.

nodes.lbl: History of recent central venous catheter

definition.val: A past medical history of a recent central venous catheter (CVC). A CVC is an indwelling device inserted into a large, central vein (most commonly the internal jugular, subclavian, or femoral) and advanced until the terminal lumen resides within the inferior vena cava, superior vena cava, or right atrium. CVCs can be a necessary producre for critically ill patients with indications such as total parenteral nutrition administration, dialysis, plasmapheresis, medication administration, and hemodynamic monitoring, and to facilitate further complex interventions such as transvenous pacemaker placement. Complications include arrhythmia, central vein stenosis, and sepsis.

nodes.lbl: History of total parenteral nutrition dependence

definition.val: A past medical history of a recent depence on total parenteral nutrition (TPN), which refers to intravenously administered nutrition being the only source of nutrition the patient is receiving.
This refers to testicular pain that is lessened or made more bearable by elevation of the testicle.

comments: Prehn sign, the relief of pain with the elevation of the testis, may be elicited in patients with epididymitis, although this is not a reliable finding.

definition.val: An abnormal enlargement or swelling localized to the abdominal wall (the skin, fascia, and muscle encases the abdominal cavity and viscera). The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.
The tympanic membrane protrudes (swells outwards). This feature may be observed with otoscopy.

comments: See Figure 1 of PMID:24134083.

nodes.lbl: Ear pain exacerbated by manipulating tragus or pinna

definition.val: Applies to pain of the ear that is worsened, aggravated, or exacerbated by touching or moving the tragus or pinna.

An abnormal enlargement or swelling localized to the side of the neck. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.
Applies to an abnormality that is situated in the occiput (back part of the head).
Abormal enlargement of the front part of the neck owing to accumulation of fluid.
Abnormal enlargement of the uvula related to an abnormal accumulation of fluid.

nodes.lbl: obsolete Purulent drainage from Stensen duct

definition.val: History of having received gastric bypass surgery. This is a procedure that reduces the functional volume of the stomach and is used to treat morbid obesity.

Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to volatile organic compounds (VOCs), which comprise various organic chemicals which are released as gases from different liquids or solids.

comments: VOCs are present in different household, industrial or commercial and products, but their accumulation in air and water has primarily gained attention. Among VOCs, trichloroethylene and vinyl chloride are the most toxic and carcinogenic compounds.

definition.val: A medical history of having undergone radiation therapy, which is a treatment that uses ionizing radiation for purposes such as the control the growth of malignant cells in cancer treatment.
Failure to record otoacoustic emissions (OAE), i.e., sounds generated from the cochlea in response to an acoustic stimulus and transmitted across the middle ear to the external ear canal.

The tympanic membrane (eardrum, myringa) is a thin, semitransparent, oval membrane, approximately 1 cm in diameter, that separates the external acoustic meatus from the tympanic cavity. Thickening refers to an increase of the dimension across the membrane.

comments: See Figure 2 of PMID:23673509.

definition.val: Filum terminale lipomas (FTLs) are a type of lumbosacral lipoma in which the fat is entirely within the filum terminale and separate from the conus medullaris.

comments: Filum terminale lipomas (FTL) are occasionally associated with tethered cord syndrome, and some authors have advocated for prophylactic sectioning of the filum terminale when an FTL is identified. With the increasing use of MRI, FTLs have been identified more frequently in asymptomatic individuals.

definition.val: The relative concentration of tetrahydrocortisol plus 5-alpha-tetrahydrocortisol relative to that of tetrahydrocortisone is below the lower limit of normal.

nodes.lbl: Anti-soluble liver antigen/liver pancreas antibody positivity

definition.val: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against soluble liver antigen.

comments: Antibodies against SLA/LP are now considered as being highly specificmarkers for auto-immune hepatitis type 1.

nodes.lbl: Anti-thrombospondin type I domain-containing 7A antibody positivity

definition.val: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against thrombospondin type I domain-containing 7A.
The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against sperm antigens.
The concentration of ficolin-3 in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

A structural abnormality of the seminal vesicle. The seminal vesicles are a pair of glands that also include the prostate gland and the bulbourethral glands and are located in the pelvis superior to the rectum, inferior to the fundus of the bladder and posterior to the prostate. The seminal vesicles contribute around 70% of the fluid that will eventually become semen.
A cyst (sac-like mass that may contain serous liquid or semisolid material) caused by distention of the seminal vesicle due to atresia of the ejaculatory duct.

comments: Congenital seminal vesical cysts are caused by altered development of the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct. They are often associated with abnormal development of other ipsilateral mesonephric derivatives, such as vas deferens, kidney, and ureter.

definition.val: History of exposure to respirable crystalline silica (SiO2).

comments: Silicosis is a well known consequence of silica dust exposure, and exposure has also been associated with the risk of lung cancer, pulmonary tuberculosis, and other airway diseases.

definition.val: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against osteoprotegerin.
A past medical history of having had a surgical procedure to remove the adrenal glands.
Activity of the enzyme mitochondrial citrate synthase (EC:2.3.3.1) in muscle tissue is above the upper limit of normal.

comments: Citrate synthase (CS) activity is a validated biomarker for mitochondrial density in skeletal muscle. CS activity is also used as a biochemical marker of the skeletal muscle oxidative adaptation to a training intervention, and a relationship between changes in whole body aerobic capacity and changes in CS activity is often assumed.

definition.val: Activity of the enzyme lactate dehdrogenase (LHD; 1.1.1.27) in muscle tissue is below the lower limit of normal. LDH catalyzes the conversion of pyruvate to lactate and back, as it converts NAD+ to NADH and back.
Activity of the enzyme Phosphoglycerate mutase (PGM) in muscle tissue is below the lower limit of normal. PGM is an enzyme that catalyzes step 8 of glycolysis (EC 5.4.2.11).
Activity of the enzyme muscle phosphorylase kinase (PhK) in muscle tissue below the lower limit of normal.

comments: The enzyme PhK comprises four copies each of four subunits (alpha, beta, gamma, and delta).

definition.val: Activity of 3-beta-hydroxysteroid-delta-5-desaturase, also known as Sterol C5-desaturase (EC 1.3.3.2), or SC5D below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.
Activity of glucose-6-phosphatase (EC 3.1.3.9) in the liver below the lower limit of normal.
Activity of glucose-6-phosphate translocase in liver below the lower limit of normal.
The presence of red blood cells (RBCs) in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). The CSF normally does not contain RBCs (erythrocytes).

comments: Erythrocytes may be seen in CSF following a traumatic lumbar tap, but in such cases RBC counts typically decrease in sequential samples. Penetration of blood into the subarachnoid space and/or CSF may be due to trauma, a ruptured aneurysm, intracerebral hemorrhage, or in connection with a tumor.

definition.val: The concentration of cholestanol in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above the upper limit of normal. Cholestanol is the 5-alpha-dihydro derivative of cholesterol.
The concentration of apolipoprotein B in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above the upper limit of normal.

nodes.lbl: Elevated CSF myelin basic protein concentration

definition.val: The concentration of myelin basic protein in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above the upper limit of normal.

synonyms.val: Myelin basic protein high in CSF

comments: Radioimmunoassay for myelin basic protein in cerebrospinal fluid is commonly used as a biochemical marker of demyelination in multiple sclerosis patients.

definition.val: The concentration of pyridoxal-5'-phosphate in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is below the lower limit of normal.
The concentration of thymine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above the upper limit of normal.
The concentration of 5-hydroxymethyluracil in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above the upper limit of normal.
The concentration of N-carbamyl-beta-aminoisobutyric acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above the upper limit of normal.
The concentration of N-carbamyl-beta-alanine in the cerebrospinal fluid is above the upper limit of normal.
The concentration of dihydrouracil in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above the upper limit of normal.
The concentration of dihydrothymine in the cerebrospinal fluid is above the upper limit of normal.
The concentration of angiotensin-converting enzyme in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

synonyms.val: Elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme level in blood
Increased angiotensin-converting enzyme level in blood

definition.val: The activity of 3-hydroxyisobutyrate dehydrogenase in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
The activity of 3-hydroxyisobutyryl-CoA hydrolase in the blood corculation is below the lower limit of normal.

nodes.lbl: Reduced HMG-CoA lyase activity in cultured fibroblasts

definition.val: Activity of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A lyase (HMG CoA lyase) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.
The activity of acyl-CoA oxidase activity in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
Activity of the enzyme xanthine oxidase (EC 1.17.3.2) below the lower limit of normal.

nodes.lbl: Reduced methylmalonate semialdehyde dehydrogenase activity in cultured fibroblasts

definition.val: The activity of methylmalonate semialdehyde dehydrogenase ( EC 1.2.1.27) in cultured fibroblasts is below the lower limit of normal.

An abnormal enlargement or swelling localized to the pharynx (i.e., the throat, the space that connects the nose and mouth to the larynx and esophagus). The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.
The presence of hidden (occult) blood in the stool.

comments: This test is commonly used for colorectal cancer screening. Blood in stool may be a sign of hemorrhoids, colorectal cancer, or another condition.

definition.val: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort that occurs when passing stool.

nodes.lbl: Recent history of caustic substance ingestion

definition.val: Medical history of a recent ingestion of a caustic substance, i.e., a highly acidic or alkaline chemicals that can cause severe burns to the mouth and digestive tract when swallowed.
Failure to pass meconium (the first stool following birth) in the first 48 hours of life.

comments: Failure to pass meconium combined with progressive abdominal distention, refusal to feed and vomiting of bilious intestinal contents are the classic clinical signs of intestinal obstruction in neonates. The first stool is passed within 24 hours of birth in 99 percent of healthy full-term infants and within 48 hours in all healthy full-term infants.

definition.val: The second sound can remain single throughout the respiratory cycle due to either absence of one component or to synchronous occurrence of the two components. Since the pulmonary vascular impedance increases with age, many normal patients over age 50 have a single S2 or at most a narrow physiologic split on inspiration because P2 occurs early. A single second sound, however, is usually due to inability to auscultate a relatively soft pulmonic component. Such inability is rare in healthy infants, children, and young adults and is uncommon even in older persons under good auscultatory conditions using a rigid stethoscopic diaphragm.
The gradient (in this case, drop) in pressure across the aortic valve is above the upper limit of normal.
A past surgical history of the implanation of an artificial heart valve.

nodes.lbl: Failure to increase oxygen saturation on hyperoxia test

definition.val: Hyperoxia test is the initial method to distinguish critical congenital heart disease (CCHD) from pulmonary disease. The test consists in measuring an arterial blood gas at room air and 100% inspired oxygen after 10 minutes. Neonates with congenital heart disease are usually not able to increase PaO2 above 100 mm Hg during 100% oxygen administration. In patients with pulmonary disease, PaO2 generally increased greater than or equal to 100 mm Hg with 100% oxygen as ventilation-perfusion discrepancies are overcome. A positive result indicates the cardiac origin and further cardiac workup is indicated to rule out CCHD.
Placement of the nipples at a higher than normal location.
The amount of calveolin-3 in muscle tissue is below the lower limit of normal.

nodes.lbl: Abnormal tissue enzyme concentration or activity

definition.val: Concentration of an enyzme in a tissue is above or between the limit of normal. This term is intended to be used for enzymes that can be measured in multiple tissues other than blood.

comments: For enzymes measured in the blood circulation, the term Abnormal circulating enzyme concentration or activity should be used.

definition.val: Cell dealth (necrosis) located in the spleen.

comments: CT of the abdomen can be used to investigate splenic necrosis.

definition.val: A carcinoid tumor of the pancreas (CTP) is a rare neuroendocrine tumor arising from the serotonin-secreting cells (enterochromaffin or Kultscitsky's cells).
The concentration of dihydroxyphenylacetic acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
Lower than appropriate concentration of acetoacetate in states such as hypoglycemia in which the normal response would be to elevate acetoacetate.

comments: Ketone synthesis in the liver produces acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate from two acetyl CoA molecules. This occurs during ketoacidosis in physiological (starvation) and disease-associated (diabetic ketoacidosis) states.

definition.val: Lower than appropriate concentration of beta-hydroxybutyrate in states such as hypoglycemia in which the normal response would be to elevate acetoacetate.

comments: Ketone synthesis in the liver produces acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate from two acetyl CoA molecules. This occurs during ketoacidosis in physiological (starvation) and disease-associated (diabetic ketoacidosis) states.

definition.val: Concentration of 3-hydroxybutyryl-carnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
The concentration of 5-amino-4-imidazolecarboxyamide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above the upper limit of normal.

nodes.lbl: Elevated circulating tumor necrosis factor alpha concentration

definition.val: The concentration of tumor necrosis factor alpha in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
The activity of concentration of pyrimidine 5-prime-nucleotidase (EC 3.1.3.5) in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

nodes.lbl: Diminished prolactin response to thyrotrophin-releasing hormone stimulation

definition.val: The increase in prolactin concentration (PRL) following stimulation with thyrotropin (thyrdoid releasing hormone) as compared to baseline PRL concentration is below the lower limit of normal.
The concentration of complement component 1s (C1s) in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
The concentration of corticosteroid-binding globulin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

synonyms.val: Decreased corticosteroid-binding globulin level in blood
Reduced corticosteroid-binding globulin level in blood

comments: Corticosteroid binding globulin (CBG) is encoded by the gene for serpin family A member 6 (SERPINA6;HGNC:1540). Cortisol transport is considered the main function of CBG. In addition to cortisol, CBG binds progesterone, aldosterone, and 11-deoxycorticosterone. It is mostly produced by the liver, up-regulated by estrogens, and suppressed by steroids. Clinically, high levels are observed in pregnancy. Low levels may be observed in patients with cirrhosis as well as with corticosteroid-binding globulin deficiency caused by variants in CBG (MIM:611489).

definition.val: The concentration of thyroglobulin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

nodes.lbl: Elevated circulating granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor concentration

definition.val: The concentration of granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

synonyms.val: Elevated circulating granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor concentration
Elevated granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor level in blood
Increased granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor level in blood

definition.val: The concentration of D-2-hydroxyglutaric acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above the upper limit of normal.
A swelling or enlargement localized to the esophagus. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.
The presence of crystals (microscopic solids that form distinct lattices, with definable fixed angles, faces, walls) in the bursa fluid.

comments: Bursa fluid is found inside bursae -small, fluid-filled sacs located around joints, especially at points of friction (e.g., between bone and tendon or skin). This feature can be ascertained by aspiration of the bursa fluid.

definition.val: Giant gastric folds are recognized at endoscopy as an increase in the size of the gastric rugae and a lack of flattening.

comments: The most common causes of giant gastric folds are Menetrier disease, acute gastric mucosal lesions, gastric lymphoma, and scirrhous carcinoma.

definition.val: The count of lymphocytes located in the epithelial layer of the gastric mucosa is above the upper limit of normal.
The count of lymphocytes located in the epithelial layer of the mucosa of the small intestine is above the upper limit of normal.
Increased response (echo) of lung tissue of a fetus observed on prenatal sonography. Increased echo response is conventially displayed as a higher degree of brightness.

comments: The ultrasonographic appearance of fetal lung hyperechogenicity is most commonly associated with congenital bronchopulmonary abnormalities, such as cystic adenomatoid malformation or pulmonary lobar sequestration.

definition.val: A histopathological finding characterized by inflammation of the arterial and/or capillary and/or venous blood vessels, leading to a change in the vascular wall as a whole.

comments: Stenosis or occlusion of the vascular lumen by thrombosis or intimal proliferation is the result of endothelial damage, which is the cause of clinical manifestations. This finding may be observed with a group of diseases including polyarteritis nodosa and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (ANCA): granulomatosis with polyangiitis, eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis, and microscopic polyangiitis.

definition.val: Any structural anomaly of the proximal convoluted tubule, which is the first tubular component of the nephron and arises as a continuation of the Bowman space from the tubular pole of the renal corpuscle. The proximal convoluted tubule is located within the renal cortex.
Presence of Leishmania, a parasitic protozoan, in a tissue specimen. Leishmania is responsible for leishmaniasis.

comments: Leishmania may be detected in tissues such as bone marrow, spleen, liver, or skin by methods including Wright or Giemsa stain.

definition.val: Demonstration of cysts of Pneumocystis (a genus of related fungal species) in respiratory secretions such as nasopharyngeal secretions or pleural fluid.
An aggregation of macrophages (forming in response to chronic inflammation) localized in or on the spinal cord.
Reduced ability to absorb folate in the diet. This finding can be measured by a folic acid loading test in which blood concentration of folate is measured after oral administration of folic acid.

Abnormally elevated quantiy of hydrogen measured by a hydrogen breath test (HBT). HBTs administer substrates such as glucose, lactulose, lactose and fructose and subsequently measure hydrogen exhaled in the breath using a gas chromatograph.

synonyms.val: Positive glucose or lactulose hydrogen breath test

comments: Bacteria, especially anaerobic, colonizing the large bowel in health and small bowel in diseased conditions produce hydrogen by fermentation of unabsorbed carbohydrates. Though small amount of hydrogen is produced from limited amounts of unabsorbed carbohydrate reaching the colon, large amounts of hydrogen may be produced if there is malaborption of carbohydrate in the small intestine allowing larger amount to reach the colon or if there is excess of bacteria in the small bowel. The hydrogen produced by the bacteria is absorbed through the wall of the small or large intestine or both. The hydrogen-containing blood travels to the lungs where the hydrogen is released and exhaled in the breath where it can be measured.

nodes.lbl: History of recent plant thorn skin puncture

definition.val: A history of a plant skin puncture preceding the current presenting condition by hours, days, or weeks.
Nondetectable kappa chain in the blood circulation.

comments: Human immunoglobulin molecules are built up by a pair of identical heavy chains, identifying the immunoglobulin class (namely Gamma, Alpha, Mu, Delta and Epsilon), and by a pair of identical light chains, Kappa or Lambda alternatively, characterizing the immunoglobulin type. In humans, under normal conditions, Kappa light chains represent approximately 2/3 of the light chains of total immunoglobulins, both circulating and lymphocyte surface bound. This terms represents a situation in which all circulating immunoglobulins have the lambda chain and none have the kappy chain. Only a few cases of K deficiency inhumans have been reported, perhaps because Kdeficiency does not have a drastic effect on the health of the individual lambda chains seem able to substitute effectively.

definition.val: A circumscribed whitish-yellow mass in the posterior chamber associated with retinal folds and sometimes retinal detachment and is said to resemble a retinal glioma.
Swelling due to fluid acculuation of the papillary dermis.

comments: The dermis has two major layers: the upper papillary dermis and the lower reticular dermis. The papillary dermis: The papillary dermis consists of bundles of collagen fibrils and oxytalan elastic fibers, ans is separated from the lower reticular dermis by a subpapillary plexus.

definition.val: The number of beats per minute (bpm) of the fetal heart is above the upper limit of the normal for the gestational age. Fetal tachycardia is thus defined as a heart rate greater than 160-180 bpm.

comments: In the first trimester of pregnancy, the fetal heart rate (FHR)increases from 125 beats per minute (bpm) at 6 weeks to about175 bpm at 9 weeks, followed by a gradual decrease to about160 bpm at 14 weeks, noted in fetuses conceived by assisted reproductive procedures.

definition.val: The amount of 3-hydroxykynurenine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
The amount of 2-oxoadipic acid in the urine, normaliyed for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
The concentration of methionine sulfoxide in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

comments: Methionine S-oxide is a derivative of methionine and is a biomarker of oxidative stress.

definition.val: The concentration of pipecolic acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
The amount of pipecolic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
Concentration of saccharopine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) above the upper limit of normal.

Concentration in the bloodstream of glycylproline above the upper limit of normal. Glycylproline is a dipeptide composed of glycine and proline, and is an end product of collagen metabolism that is further cleaved by prolidase (EC 3.4.13.9).
The concentration of octanoylcarnitine (C8:0) in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

comments: C8: octanoylcarnitine high in blood

definition.val: The concentration of decanoylcarnitine (C10:0) in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
Increased concentration of 2-hydroxyphenylacetic acid in the urine.
Amount of 4-hydroxyphenyllactic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
The concentration of beta-alanine present in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above the upper limit of normal.
The concentration of 2-aminoadipic acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
The amount of N-carbamoyl-beta-alanine present in urine, when adjusted for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
Concentration of cystathionine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) above the upper limit of normal.
The amount of gamma-glutamylphenylalanine in the urine, when normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
Concentration of aspartylglucosamine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
The amount of saccharopine in the urine, when normalized to urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
Abnormal increase in size of the tectal plate (also known as the tectum or the quadrigeminal plate). The tectum is the dorsal portion of the midbrain (brainstem).

A swelling or enlargement localized to the retroperitoneal region. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.
A lighter than expected T1 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brainstem. This term refers to a localized hyperintensity affecting a particular region of the brainstem.
A type of fracture that occurs in the trabecular cancellous bone just beneath the subchondral bone plate without disruption of the articular surface.

An abscess (i.e., a circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris) localized in the area surrounded by the deep fascia of the neck including the pharynx, larynx, trachea, upper esophagus, thyroid, and parathyroid glands. Infections of pharyngeal, tonsillar, and laryngeal origin affect this space, which includes the parapharyngeal and retropharyngeal spaces.
Anlarged and edematous epiglottis. This sign can be observed on a lateral radiograph of the neck and it suggests a diagnosis of acute infectious epiglottitis.

Increase in the anterior posterior dimension of the prevertebral space, which is located in the neck region between the anterior part of the cervical spine and the deep layer of the deep cervical fascia running between the transverse processes of the spine.
Increase in diameter of the third cranial nerve (oculomotor nerve). This feature can be observed by magnetic resonance imaging and may be accompanied by contrast enhancement.
Concentration of sphoingomyelin in tissues above the upper limit of normal.

nodes.lbl: History of recent iodated contrast medium administration

definition.val: Medical history of recent iodinated or radioiodine contrast use.

comments: Iodinated contrast media commonly used in various radiologic examinations and interventional procedures results in massive iodide exposure to the thyroid gland. Whereas people with normal thyroids usually experience no ill effects, those with pre-existing thyroid disease may experience thyrotoxicosis (often referred to as thyroid storm in this context), which, if unrecognized, could lead to serious, potentially life-threatening consequences, including atrial arrhythmias, heart failure, pulmonary arterial hypertension, cerebrovascular and pulmonary embolism, and cardiomyopathy.

definition.val: Difficulty inserting a nasogastric tube (NGT), a flexible plastic tube that is placed through the nose and esophagus into the stomach and used to administer drugs or for feeding. There are certain circumstances that may make NGT insertion difficult. They are esophageal narrowing, comatose or intubated patients, and patients who have sustained severe facial or skull injuries.

A falcine sinus that does not involute but persists beyond birth is defined as a persistent falcine sinus. In the 20-mm embryo stage, the primitive falx cerebri contains the sagittal plexus, a meshwork of anastomotic venous channels from which the superior sagittal sinus and straight sinus are thought to develop. A persistent falcine sinus represents a persistent channel of the caudal anastomotic loops of the sagittal plexus.
A medical history in a male of not having been circumcized.

comments: Neonatal male circumcision is a common surgical procedure.

definition.val: A medical history of use of facial makeup.

comments: Facial makeup use may be associated with canaliculitis, which refers to inflammation of the lacrimal canaliculus.

definition.val: A feeling of clicking or snapping at the knuckle (metacarpophalangeal joint) upon extension of flexion of the finger.
An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the forearm.
A type of displaced fracture in which there has been a rotation of the distal fracture fragment in relation to the proximal portion.
Applies to an abnormality that is situated on the skin in areas where bones are close to the surface (bony prominences).
A past medical history of wearing tight shoes, toe-box shoes, or high heel shoes.

comments: This may be a risk factor for Morton neuroma.

definition.val: Reduced skin turgor means reduced elastic recoil of the skin to its normal contour after being pinched in a fold.
Medical history of recently eating wild mushrooms.
Refers to symptomatology that begins in the proximal limbs and subsequently affects the distal limbs.

The selective paralysis of voluntary fascio-pharyngo-glosso-masticatory movements with preservation of reflexive and automatic functions is referred to as autonomic-voluntary dissociation, which is a distinctive feature of Anterior opercular syndrome (also known as Foix-Chavany-Marie syndrome).

comments: The patient cannot open or close the mouth, protrude the tongue or close the eyes to orders, but can smile, cry, yell or yawn automatically. Ischemia is the most frequent cause and it is generally due to bilateral opercular lesions, but bilateral subcortical lesions have also been reported. In the anterior opercular syndrome the connections be-tween the motor cortex and the V, VII, IX, XII cranial nuclei and brainstem are interrupted bilaterally. Emotional and spontaneous movements, dependent on extrapyramidal connections, thalamus and hypothalamus, are preserved (automatic-voluntary dissociation).

definition.val: A swelling or enlargement localized to the jaw. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.
Exposure to continuous light at night, including night-shift work or a nocturnal lifestyle.

nodes.lbl: Menstruating female between menarche and menopause

definition.val: Past medical history of a woman who is menstruating, i.e., not premenstrual or post-menopause.
PPROM (preterm premature rupture of membranes) occurs at less than 37 weeks of gestation. PPROM can happen spontaneously, during preterm labor, or following a procedure such as amniocentesis.
A past medical history that indicates that the patient had a surgical procedure involving the abdomen.
The thickness of the Descement membrane is above the upper limit of normal.

Right bundle branch block (RBBB) represents an abnormality in the intraventricular electrical conduction system of the human heart, generating enlarged QRS and modified vectors on the electrocardiogram (ECG). Incomplete RBBB (IRBBB) is defined by (i) QRS duration between 110 and 120 ms in adults; (ii) rsr, rsR, or rSR in leads V1 or V2. The R or r deflection is usually wider than the initial R wave. In a minority of patients, a wide and often notched R wave pattern may be seen in leads V1 and/or V2; (iii) S wave of greater duration than R wave or greater than 40 ms in leads I and V6 in adults; and (iv) Normal R peak time in leads V5 and V6 but greater than 50 ms in lead V1.
