comments: Bone scintigraphy is frequently performed as part of the routine staging of patients with a wide variety of primary malignancies. Although it is a sensitive imaging modality, it is relatively nonspecific, and there are many potential causes of increased isotope uptake that can mimic metastatic disease.

nodes.lbl: Diminished long-chain-enoyl-CoA hydratase activity in cultured fibroblasts

definition.val: Concentration or activity of long-chain-enoyl-CoA hydratase (EC 4.2.1.74) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

nodes.lbl: Diminished acetyl-CoA C-acyltransferase activity in cultured fibroblasts

definition.val: Concentration or activity of acetyl-CoA C-acyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.16) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal. This enzyme catalyzes the reaction acetyl-CoA + an acyl-CoA = a 3-oxoacyl-CoA + CoA. It is also known as 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase and beta-ketothiolase.

synonyms.val: Reduced 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase activity in cultured fibroblasts

definition.val: Pathological inclusion bodies are are composed of glycogen, proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, hemosiderin, and calcium, that accumulate as metabolic by-products, catabolic products of macromolecular complexes, or in the context of cell injury.

nodes.lbl: Reduced epidermal collagen IV alpha 5 chain staining

definition.val: Diminished or absent collagen alpha5(IV) chain staining pattern in the epidermal basement membrane.

nodes.lbl: Diminished glomerular basement membrane collagen IV alpha 3 chain staining

definition.val: Abnormal reduction in the amount of the alpha 3 chain of collagen IV in the basement membrane of the glomeruli of the kidney.

nodes.lbl: Diminished glomerular basement membrane collagen IV alpha 4 chain staining

definition.val: Abnormal reduction in the amount of the alpha 4 chain of collagen IV in the basement membrane of the glomeruli of the kidney.

nodes.lbl: Diminished glomerular basement membrane collagen IV alpha 5 chain staining

definition.val: Abnormal reduction in the amount of the alpha 5 chain of collagen IV in the basement membrane of the glomeruli of the kidney.

A cystine stone is a type of kidney stone that is yellowish brown with a granular surface. They are observed in individuals with Cystinuria and tend to be of early onset, to occur repeatedly, and to be associated with urinary tract infections.

synonyms.val: Yellowish brown character to kidney stone suggestive of cystine

definition.val: Accumulation of cystine in the liver.

comments: Cystine crystal accumulation activates Kupffer cells and secreted vasoactive substances cause vasoconstriction in microcirculation resulting in portal hypertension

definition.val: The presence of cystine crystals in bone marrow cells as demonstrated in a fresh bone marrow aspiration sample.

Desmoid tumors are rare, locally aggressive, fibroblastic soft-tissue tumors that are characterized by infiltrative growth and tendency to recur. Desmoid tumors do not metastasize but can arise in any part of the body: extra-abdominal (appear in the head and neck, chest, extremities), and abdominal wall or intra-abdominal (originating in tissue that connects abdominal organs).
A segment of the jejunum that runs parallel to the normal jejunum and communicates with the jejunal lumen at one or both ends.
A full thickness tear or breakage of the myocardium of the left ventricle.
Multiple punctate (speckled, patchy spot-like) and/or curvilinear areas of gadolinium enhancement distributed around blood vessels in the pons.

comments: The lesions may extend into adjacent CNS structures, caudally to the medulla oblongata or the cervicothoracal spinal cord, rostrally to the midbrain, and even involve supratentorial regions such as the thalami, capsula interna, basal ganglia, corpus callosum and cerebral white matter. See Figure 1 of PMID:24028073.

definition.val: Presence of one or more adult worms in the intestine as demonstrated by sonography or passage of a worm in the stool. On sonography, worms may appear as linear, echogenic structures within the intestines.
Demonstration of one or more worms in the scrotum. This finding can be appreciated by sonography, where echogenic, linear structures could be seen moving within the scrotum.
A small bowel tumor with adenomatous epithelium.

comments: Grossly and histologically, adenomas arising in the mucosa of the small intestine are similar to the adenomas found in the colon.

definition.val: Mottling (spots or blotches with different shades) of the retinal pigment epithelium in the mother of the index patient. Retinal mottling may indicate a mosaic X-linked inactivation state in the mother.

A stretched conical-shaped structure found at the gallbladder neck with several linear echoes converging towards its tip. This finding is demonstrated by sonography and can indicate gallbladder volvulus.

synonyms.val: Conical structure at the gallbladder neck

definition.val: Fistula between the gallbladder and the intestine.
Impaired ability to accurately measure or estimate time intervals.

comments: Common signs of dyschronometria are often generic to cerebellar ataxia, including a lack of spatial awareness, poor short term memory, and inability to keep track of time. For example, when asked to wait for thirty seconds, or tap every second that has gone by, those affected will be able to perform the task for a short time and then become derailed. This can result from a loss of focus, however, more often than not the individual affected can no longer tell what they are doing and they become disoriented. This often takes form in forgetting basic time keeping unless a timer is set, such as when cooking for example. Dyschronometria does not affect the 24-hour circadian rhythm, which is sustained by a different biological process.

definition.val: History of recently intermittent breastfeeding an infant (i.e., on and off).

comments: Recent on and off breastfeeding can be a risk factor for galactocele and breast abscess.

definition.val: A benign, fluid-filled sac in the breast.
Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance are well-defined and localized to a specific area.
Applies to an abnormality that displays multiple indentations and/or elevations producing an irregular surface contour.
Applies to an abnormality with irregular, radiating, or spiky edges.

comments: A spiculated mass is a centrally dense lesion seen on mammography with sharp lines radiating from its margin. The spicules can vary greatly in length, from a few millimeters to several centimeters. In malignant lesions, spicules represent a mixture of tumor cells and fibrosis invading the normal tissue surrounding the lesion.

definition.val: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance resembles series of a concentric circles or spirals.
Delta brushes are transient patterns characterised by a slow delta wave with superimposed fast activity.

comments: Delta brushes are the hallmark of the EEG of premature infants.

definition.val: Fusion of the junction between the distal tibia, fibula and the talus.
he term given when a vertebral body has lost almost its entire height anteriorly and posteriorly, representing a very advanced compression fracture.
An abnormal gait caused by a rotational variation anywhere in the lower extremity that causes the foot to point inward, instead of pointing straight ahead or outward, when walking or running.

comments: The three major causes of pediatric in-toeing are metatarsus adductus, internal tibial torsion, and femoral anteversion.

definition.val: A vibration felt upon palpation of a blood vessel over an extremity.

comments: This feature can be due to an arteriovenous malformation.

definition.val: The feet turn excessively outward when walking, caused by a rotational variation in the leg.
An abnormal separation between the talo-tibial joint.
The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against neuronal intermediate filament.
The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against dendritic spine scaffolding protein Drebrin.
The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against anti-lipoprotein lipase.
The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against apoCII.
The presence of intracellular inclusion bodies (aggregates of stainable substances, usually proteins) in neurons that stain with eosin, a red or pink dye.
A characteristic smell said to resemble the odor of dirty socks.

comments: This feature is characteristic of isoveleric acidemia.

definition.val: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against acetylcholine receptor.

comments: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (AChR) are ligand-gated cation channels that are present throughout the nervous system. The muscle AChR mediates transmission at the neuromuscular junction; antibodies against the muscle AChR are the cause of myasthenia gravis. The ganglionic (alpha 3-type) neuronal AChR mediates fast synaptic transmission in sympathetic, parasympathetic, and enteric autonomic ganglia. Impaired cholinergic ganglionic synaptic transmission is one important cause of autonomic failure.

definition.val: Applies to an abnormality that is located on hair shafts.

nodes.lbl: Prolonged use of tightly fitting footwear

definition.val: History of use of tightly fitting shoes for a long period of time.

comments: This may be a risk factor for tinea pedis.

definition.val: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about ingestion of high quantities of protein.

comments: Metabolic triggers for late-onset urea cycle disorders include excessive protein intake.

definition.val: An abnormally increased thickness of a leaflet of the tricuspid valve.
Abnormal shifting of the anterior fontanelle fropm its normal central position.

comments: This feature can be related to an abnormality of the cranial sutures, mostly craniosynostosis.

definition.val: Accumulation of cerebral spinal fluid in the subdural space.

Incus ankylosis refers to congenital or acquired fixation of the incus, which is associated with conductive hearing resulting from impairment of the sound-conduction mechanism (the external auditory canal, tympanic membrane, and/or middle-ear ossicles).
A tendency to reject a variety of foods and/or to eat a restricted range of foods.
Dyskinesis is used to describe ventricular muscle segments that bulge outside the left ventricular cavity during systole, as opposed to contracting inwards with the rest of the segments.
A longitudinal red band extending from the proximal nail fold or lunula to the distal nail plate.
Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by exposure to sunlight.
Applied to a sign or symptom that is made worse by exposure to heat (high ambient temperatures).
Applied to a sign or symptom that is made worse by excessive sweating.

comments: High temperatures, high humidity, excessive sweating can exacerbate cutaneous wounds.

definition.val: The accumulation of a significant amount of exudate in the pleural space, accompanied by the presence of malignant cells or tumour tissue.

nodes.lbl: Inappropriately low urine osmolality following challenge

definition.val: In diabetes insipidus, affected individuals produce large quantities of dilute urine. In nephrogenic DI, the kidneys do not respond to vasopressin. In a water deprivation test or with administration of exogenous vasopressin, the osmolaltiy of the urine does not increase as normally.

nodes.lbl: Reduced urine tetrahydrocortisol plus 5-alpha-THF to tetrahydrocortisone ratio

definition.val: Abnormally low ratio of tetrahydrocortisol (THF) plus 5-alpha-THF to tetrahydrocortisone (THE).

comments: In cortisone reductase deficiency-2, the ratio of tetrahydrocortisol (THF) plus 5-alpha-THF to tetrahydrocortisone (THE), which in CORTRD patients is typically less than 0.1 (reference range, 0.7 to 1.2).

definition.val: The amount of 2,4-dihydroxyglutarate in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

An abnormal result of the xylose absorption test that is used to assess the ability of the intestines to absorb D-xylose. D-xylose is a five-carbon monosaccharide found in some plants. The patient drinks a solution containing a specific amount of D-xylose and the concentration of xylose is measured in the blood circulation and then in the urine. A low amount of D-xylose indicates reduced small intestinal absorbtion.

comments: The standard 25-g D-xylose test in adults, based on analysis of a 5-h urine collection and a 1-h serum sample, discriminates between normal subjects and patients with proximal small intestinal malabsorption with X5% specificity and sensitivity.

definition.val: An abnormal growth or accumulation of tissue in a hemisphere of the cerebrum. Typically a mass is an initial finding that will lead to additional workup.
Increased signal on T2 magnetic resonance imaging characterized by a linear region of high signal surrounding the lateral aspect of the putamen at 1.5 Tesla.
An abnormal growth or accumulation of tissue in the posterior fossa, affecting the cerebellum or fourth ventricle. Typically a mass is an initial finding that will lead to additional workup.
Abnormal increased variability in the timing between consecutive R-waves on an electrocardiogram.

comments: Sinus arrhythmia is a variation of normal sinus rhythm that characteristically presents with an irregular rate in which the change in the R-R interval is greater than 0.12 seconds.

definition.val: Abnormally increased variability in the timing between consecutive P-waves on an electrocardiogram.
Demonstration of fungi growing on hair by a method such as microscopy of hairs mounted on slides with 10% potassium hydroxide.
A past medical history of having long, full hair.

fine white linear scars under intact conjunctival epithelium. This scarring appears in areas of previous conjunctival ulceration or pseudomembrane formation, weeks to months after the insult is healed.

comments: Subepithelial fibrosis can be a manifestation of ocular graft-versus-host disease (oGVHD), but can also be found after epidemic keratoconjunctivitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and chemical burns.

definition.val: Abnormal reduction in depth of the fornix of the conjunctiva. The fornix is the area where the conjunctiva folds back upon itself, thereby creating a recessed space.
History of exposure to ultraviolet light, such as may be encountered with outdoor activities, living near equator, radiation.
A history of intravaginal cleansing with a liquid solution for personal hygiene or aesthetic reasons.

comments: Douching represents a risk factor for bacterial vaginosis.

nodes.lbl: Exposure to oily lotions or creams

definition.val: A history of applying oily lotions or creams to the skin.

comments: This may be a risk factor for tinea versicolor.

nodes.lbl: Elevated circulating pristanic acid concentration following branched-chain fatty acid ingestion

definition.val: Concentration of pristanic acid in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. This finding can be observed in Zellweger syndrome. Note that branched-chain fatty acid accumulation depends on dietary intake of phytanic acid, which is minimal in formula- and breast-fed infants. Thus, phytanic and pristanic acid levels are normal in a neonate with Zellweger spectrum disorder.

nodes.lbl: Decreased CD4+ T cell ZAP-70 protein expression

definition.val: Reduction in the level of ZAP-70 protein CD4-positive T cells.

synonyms.val: Decreased T-cell ZAP-70 protein expression in CD4-positive T cells

comments: Testing of CD4+ T cells reveals absence or near absence of ZAP-70 protein in most individuals affected by ZAP70-related combined immunodeficiency.

nodes.lbl: Dorsal flexion contracture of the ankle

definition.val: A type of contracture in which the dorsal flexion muscles of the ankle are contracted.

comments: Dorsiflexion of the ankle is the movement of the top of the foot towards the leg in an upward motion. With dorsal flexion contracture, the ability to passively or actively move the tip of the toe away from the leg is limited.

definition.val: Lack of the normal diaphyseal constriction (thinning of long bones toward the midshaft area) giving the submetaphyseal areas an abnormally wide appearance.
Compression of the common iliac vein against the spine by the contralateral common iliac artery.

comments: Pulsations of the overriding artery cause shear stress and endothelial changes in the vein, resulting in the formation of fibrous bands or spurs. Over time, the affected area forms a stricture, causing impaired venous return and, in some circumstances, deep venous thrombosis. Common iliac vein compression can be ascertained by Doppler sonography.

definition.val: Detection of abnormal amyloid deposits in the body by 123I-labeled serum amyloid P component (SAP) scintigraphy.
Motor and/or sensory cranial nerve findings ipsilateral to the lesion, and at the same time motor and/or sensory findings on the contralateral side of the body.
Reduced ability to inflate the cheeks by blowing air into them while keeping the lips closed.

comments: This feature may be related to facial muscle weakness as well as to cranial nerve VII lesions.

definition.val: Visual sensations caused by changes within the eye itself, rather than by the normal light stimulation process. Entoptic phenomena are classified in the syndrome as floaters, blue field entoptic phenomenon, photopsia and self-light of the eye.

An abnormality of the vestibulospinal (VS) reflexes, which contribute to the control of postural orientation. In this task, they continuously collaborate with reflexes elicited by stimulation of visual and somatosensory receptors. Labyrinthine receptors are sensitive to modifications (i) of the head position with respect to the earth vertical or (ii) of the angular/linear velocity of head motion in space. This information can be used to monitor deviations from the maintained body position.

An abnormal result of the probe-to-bone (PTB) test. The PTB test is performed by inserting a sterile, metal surgical probe into the ulcer and is positive if a hard, gritty surface is felt inside. For large wounds, this may require gentle exploration of the wound with the probe.

comments: The basis behind the PTB test is that if a probe can reach bone, so can bacteria.

definition.val: A history of exposure to repetitive impact on palm or hand, such as working with a jackhammer.

comments: This history can be a risk factor for carpal tunnel syndrome.

definition.val: A partial or complete breakage of the scaphoid bone.
Resistance to the effects of local anaesthesia, with delayed onset or failure of local anesthetics to incude numbness or relieve pain.

comments: This feature has been reported in individuals with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

definition.val: Applied to lesions whose distribution is confined or restricted to the palms of the hands and soles of the feet.
A raised, flat-topped lesion with a diameter of one centimeter or more that is located in the mucosa of the mouth.

nodes.lbl: Positive saliva rabies nucleic acid test

definition.val: Detection of rabies nucleic acid in saliva by a method such as polymerase chain reaction.
Activity of arylsulfatase A (EC 3.1.6.8) above the upper limit of normal. The activity can be measured in multiple tissues including culutured fibroblasts and leukocytes or in the blood circulation.
The concentration of a methysterol in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

comments: This group of compounds includes thje 4-alpha-monomethyl sterols and 4,4-prime-dimethyl sterols.

definition.val: The amount of adipic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal. Adipic acid is an alpha,omega-dicarboxylic acid that is the 1,4-dicarboxy derivative of butane.
Slow-wave activity observed in the temporal area of the scalp electro-encephalogram (EEG).

synonyms.val: EEG with slow activity in temporal lobes
EEG with slow-wave activity involving the temporal lobes

nodes.lbl: History of high-pressure injection injury of the hand

definition.val: Medical history of the hand having come into contact with the nozzle of a high-pressure injecting system such as a paint gun or air compressor.
Excessively long styloid process of the ulna.

comments: Ulnar styloid impaction syndrome involves impaction between the tip of the ulnar styloid process and the triquetrum bone. This syndrome is most commonly seen in patients with excessively long or hypertrophic ulnar styloid processes and is not necessarily associated with positive ulnar variance. The ulnar styloid process index (USPI), calculated as the difference between the ulnar styloid length and the ulnar variance divided by the transverse diameter of the ulnar head, is commonly used to assess the size of the ulnar styloid. An excessively long ulnar styloid has a length greater than 6 mm or a USPI more than 0.21. Repetitive friction of the proximal pole of the triquetrum and the ulnar styloid tip leads to chondromalacia, synovitis, and ulnar-sided wrist pain.

nodes.lbl: History of recent peripheral venous catheter

definition.val: A history of placement of a peripehral venous catheter in the hours, days, or weeks before the current presenting complaint.
Exudation of a thick, opaque fluid from a wound or skin lesion, typically as a result of infection and draining pus, i.e., dead white blood cells, bacteria, and tissue debris.

nodes.lbl: Occupational history of putting fingers in other people's mouths

definition.val: A history of exposure of fingers by putting them in other peoples' mouths occupationally, e.g., as a dentist or physician.

comments: This is a risk factor for Herpetic whitlow.

definition.val: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance are limited to or predominantly affect a single finger.
Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance affect more than one finger.

nodes.lbl: Pain disproportionate to abnormality on physical exam

definition.val: Exquisite tenderness in a specific region, beyond what one would surmise from examination.

comments: This finding may be observed with several diseases including necrotizing fasciitis and gas gangrene.

definition.val: Hypoplasia or aplasia of the greater or lesser wing of the sphenoid bone, typically resulting in widening of the superior orbital fissure, elevation of the [lesser sphenoid wing, and ipsilateral orbital enlargement.

comments: All reported cases of congenital sphenoid wing dysplasia have been attributed to neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1). Sphenoid bone dysplasia occurs in 3-11 percent of the subjects with neurofibromatosis type 1 NF1 patients. This malformation, a distinctive diagnostic feature for NF1, is characterized by progressive proptosis and facial disfiguration secondary to herniation of meningeal and cerebral structures. Unilateral in most of the cases, sphenoid bone dysplasia associated with plexiform neurofibroma in the territory of the trigeminal nerve in several cases and pooling of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in all cases often described in the past as an arachnoid cyst.

definition.val: An injury in which skin and underlying tissues are cut or torn.
A partial or complete breakage of a metacarpal bone.

nodes.lbl: Pain at the base of the thumb

definition.val: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort localized to the base of the thumb, over thenar eminence or thumb metacarpal.

comments: The base of the thumb is the fleshy area on the palm side of the hand near where the thumb attaches to the hand.

nodes.lbl: History of recent participation in athletics

definition.val: Medical history of participation in sports (football, basketball, soccer, skiing) in the hours, days, or weeks prior to the current presenting complaint.
History of trauma months to years ago, including but not limited to fracture or other orthopedic injury at the symptomatic area.

comments: This feature may suggest scaphoid nonunion advanced collapse, scapholunate advanced collapse, or distal radioulnar joint arthritis.

definition.val: An inflammatory condition of the joint that connects the far ends of the radius and the ulna, known as the distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ). DRUJ arthritis may be characterized by widening of the DRUJ interval, volar/dorsal displacement of the distal ulna, radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis at the DRUJ joint including osteophytes, subchondral cysts, subchrondal sclerosis, and joint space narrowing.

synonyms.val: Arthritis of the distal radioulnar joint

comments: Arthritis of the distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ) between the sigmoid notch of the distal radius and the ulnar head can be caused by traumatic, inflammatory, congenital, and degenerative processes.

definition.val: Fracture of the proximal end of the radius involving the radial head.

An injury to the lateral collateral ligament (LCL) of the elbow. The LCL is a complex capsuloligamentous structure critical in stabilizing the ulnohumeral and radiocapitellar articulations. LCL injury can result in elbow instability, allowing the proximal radius and ulna to externally rotate away from the humerus as a supination stress is applied to the forearm.

synonyms.val: Ligamentous tear on the lateral aspect of the elbow

definition.val: An injury to the medial collateral ligament (MCL) of the elbow.

synonyms.val: Ligamentous tear on the medial aspect of the elbow

comments: Elbow medial collateral ligament sprain occurs when the elbow is subjected to a valgus force exceeding the tensile properties of the medial collateral ligament (MCL). This is an injury seen more often in throwing athletes.

definition.val: Fracture of the coronoid process on the proximal ulna.

comments: The coronoid process acts to buttress against the posterior translation of the ulna on the humerus. It is also the attachment site for the anterior elbow capsule, brachialis, and the medial collateral ligament of the elbow. Coronoid fractures are critical injuries and are suggestive of elbow instability.

definition.val: A medical history of hving had a spinal cord injury prior to the presenting complaint.

comments: Spinal cord injury (SCI) results from direct or indirect spinal cord damage. The most common SCI cause is acute trauma from motor vehicular crashes (MVCs), although the condition may also arise from insidious etiologies such as malignancies and chronic tuberculous infection. Spinal cord lesions may lead to permanent disability, significant morbidity, and even mortality. High spinal injuries often impair cardiorespiratory function, requiring emergent interventions.

definition.val: Paresthesias in anterior/medial aspect of the thigh (anterior and medial cutaneous nerves of the thigh) and/or medial aspect of the lower leg and foot (saphenous distribution). May be accompanied by weakness in the quadriceps.
Breakage (tear) of the triceps tendon.
History of having been treateed with digoxin.

comments: Digoxin is a cardiac glycoside derived from the foxglove plant (digitalis species). It has inotropic effects and is utilized in the management of systolic dysfunction in patients with congestive heart failure (CHF) and as an atrioventricular nodal blocking agent for managing atrial tachydysrhythmias. Gastrointestinal upset is the most common symptom of digoxin toxicity. Patients also may report visual symptoms, which classically present as a yellow-green discoloration, and cardiovascular symptoms, such as palpitations, dyspnea, and syncope.

definition.val: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the upper arm.

comments: Pain anywhere between the shoulder and elbow. Upper arm pain may be observed with conditions such as ulnar shaft fracture, intersection syndrome of hand tendons, Galeazzi fracture, radial tunnel syndrome, and wrist dislocation.

definition.val: A partial or complete breakage of the capitulum of the humerus, which is a smooth, rounded eminence on the lateral portion of the distal articular surface of the humerus.
An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the anterior (front) part of the shoulder.

comments: Pain localized to the anterior aspect of the shoulder. Anterior shoulder pain may be observed in conditions such as proximal biceps tendon tear.

nodes.lbl: Pain at the anterior aspect of the elbow

definition.val: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the front part of the elbow front part of the elbow, that is, on the ventral side of the arm where the arm bends.

nodes.lbl: Posterior fat pad sign of the elbow

definition.val: Lateral elbow x-ray showing lucent crescent of fat that indicates a joint effusion in the elbow .

nodes.lbl: Pain at the anterior aspect of the knee

definition.val: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the front part of the knee, that is, the side of the knee where the patella is located.

nodes.lbl: Pain at the posterior aspect of the knee

definition.val: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the back part of the knee, that is, opposite to the side of the knee where the patella is located.

comments: Pain at the posterior aspect of the knee may be observed with Baker cyst.

definition.val: Biceps tendinitis is inflammation of the tendon around the long head of the biceps muscle.

comments: MRI may show increased T2 signal around the biceps tendon or ultrasound showing thickening of the biceps tendon.

nodes.lbl: Increased peripheral nerve cross sectional area

definition.val: Ultrasonography showing increased cross sectional area (CSA) of a peripheral nerve as it travels through a potential site of compression.

comments: This feature may be observed in conditions such as carpal tunnel syndrome, ulnar tunnel syndrome, cubital tunnel syndrome, and radial tunnel syndrome.

nodes.lbl: Pain exacerbated by passive flexion at joint

definition.val: Pain in extremity that worsens with joint is passively flexed.

comments: This feature may be observed in acute compartment syndrome.

nodes.lbl: Positive hook test at the elbow

definition.val: With forearm fully supinated and elbow flexed to 90 degrees, examiner hooks a finger a bit around the distal biceps tendon at the anterior aspect of the elbow. Test is positive when there is lack of appreciable cord like structure to hook around.

comments: This sign can indicate a distal biceps tendon tear.

definition.val: Manual downward pressure on the arm with the shoulders flexed forward to 90 degrees, elbows fully extended, and palm facing up recreates pain in the anterior shoulder region; named after Dr. Speed.

comments: The Speed's test was recorded as positive if the patient experienced pain in the proximal portion of the shoulder during the application of a downward force applied to the arm. The patient's arm was placed with the forearm in full supination at 90 degrees of shoulder elevation. See Figure 1 of PMID:9848587.

definition.val: A disruption of the greater and lesser arcs of the lunate bone, with the lunate having a triangular silhouette, know as the piece of pie sign. Often caused by falling on an outstretched hand, patients will have tenderness to palpation over the dorsum of the wrist and may have sensory deficits in the median nerve distribution.

synonyms.val: Piece of pie sign of lunate bone

comments: See Figure 3 of PMID:23616330.

definition.val: Pain worsens with wrist ulnar or radial deviation.

comments: Ulnar: Triangular fibrocartilage complex tear; Ulnocarpal abutment syndrome Radial: Triangular fibrocartilage complex tear.

nodes.lbl: Pain on the lateral aspect of the foot

definition.val: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the side of the foot nearest to the little (fifth) toe.

nodes.lbl: Pain at the medial aspect of the knee

definition.val: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the inner side of knee, that is, the region of the knee that faces the other knee.

comments: This feature may be observed with medial collateral ligament knee injury.

nodes.lbl: Pain at the lateral aspect of the knee

definition.val: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the outer side of knee, that is, the region of the knee that faces away from the other knee.

comments: This feature may be observed with lateral collateral ligament injury.

definition.val: A history of exposure to frequent squatting/kneeling and/or heavy lifting.

comments: Occupations that require frequent kneeling such as roofing, construction workers, plumbers, electricians, landscapers, gardeners, carpenters, and housekeepers may increase risk of prepatellar bursitis and knee osteoarthritis.

definition.val: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the structures around the greater trochanter (the bony prominence on the outer part of the femur).

synonyms.val: Pain at the lateral aspect of the hip
Pain on the outside of the hip

definition.val: A noticeable lump or swelling in the arm or leg that you can feel with you fingers and this lump is beating or pulsating, similar to the feeling of a heartbeat.

comments: This finding may be observed with conditions such as arteriovenous malformation located in the arm or leg or withulnar artery thrombosis.

definition.val: Any anomaly of the R wave of the EKG, which is the first upward deflection after the P wave. The R wave reflects early ventricular depolarisation.
Absence of the normal increase in size of the R wave in the precordial leads when advancing from lead V1 to V6 of the electrocardiogram.

comments: With normal R wave progression, the amplitude of the R wave gradually increased from V1 to V5 and decreases from V5 to V6. Abnormal R wave progression may be observed with myocardial infarction, cardiomyopathy, right or left ventricular hypertrophy, and other conditions.

definition.val: The R wave in leads V1-V2 is normally considerably smaller in amplitude than the S wave in the same leads. Prominent R wave in these leads implies the R wave is larger than the S-wave, which may indicate cardiovascular pathology. This term includes Tall R wave in lead V1, which is defined by a R/S ratio greater than 1.

synonyms.val: High voltage R wave in V1/V2
Prominent R wave in lead V1

comments: This electrocardiographic finding exists as a normal variant in only 1% of patients. Physicians should therefore be familiar with the differential diagnosis for this important QRS configuration. The electrocardiographic entities which can present with this finding include right bundle branch block, left ventricular ectopy, right ventricular hypertrophy, acute right ventricular dilation (acute right heart strain), type a Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, posterior myocardial infarction, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, progressive muscular dystrophy, dextrocardia, misplaced precordial leads, and normal variant.

definition.val: An abnormal enlargement or swelling localized to a finger.

comments: The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

definition.val: An abnormal enlargement or swelling localized to a foot.

comments: The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

definition.val: A condition characterized by structural abnormalities of the retinal veins, including tortuosity, dilation, narrowing, or irregularities in branching patterns. These changes may be associated with systemic or ocular diseases such as retinal vein occlusion, diabetic retinopathy, or hypertensive retinopathy.

Spongiosis refers to the increased intercellular edema in the epidermis resulting in the pulling away of the keratinocytes from their surrounding desmosomes. Histologically, the spongiotic tissue reaction pattern involves the accumulation of fluid in the intercellular spaces of the epidermis, making the desmosomes junctions more easy to appreciate. Parakeratosis forms above the areas of spongiosis. The foci of spongiosis can be microscopic to grossly identifiable clinically with vesicles or bullae.

comments: Comment: Spongiosis is present in all diseases manifesting clinically as eczema; however, there are diseases with spongiosis that do not belong to the eczema spectrum, e.g., pityriasis rosea, erysipelas or tinea. . Spongiotic dermatoses include a very large list of disorders which are best grouped under neutrophilic, eosinophilic, miliarial, follicular and pityriasiform forms of spongiosis.

definition.val: A congenital finding where the adrenal gland does not form it's typical triangular, Y or V shape and is instead discoid, straight or elongated in shape. It is often found incidentally on renal ultrasound and is associated with renal agenesis and other renal congenital anomalies.
A structural abnormality in the blood vessels of the optic disc, including bleeding, tortuosity, dilation, shunting, or other unusual branching patterns.

comments: May be associated with conditions such as glaucoma, papilledema, leber optic neuropathy, or optic disc drusen, and can contribute to visual field defects or other optic neuropathies.

definition.val: Localization of symptoms such as numbness or paresthesias on the skin over the upper chest, specifically above the clavicle and over the lateral aspect of the neck, corresponding to the distribution of the supraclavicular nerve.

comments: May be observed with clavicle shaft fracture.

definition.val: Difficulty rotating the lower part of the arm towards the body (tested with the elbow flexed and the elbow held next to the side of the body or shoulder 90 degrees abducted to the side) secondary to pain, weakness, or mechanical block.

comments: Conditions characterized by this finding include shoulder internal impingement syndrome, pectoralis major rupture, proximal humeral epiphysiolysis, and rotator cuff tear arthropathy.

nodes.lbl: Superior displacement of the humeral head

definition.val: An anterior posterior (AP) shoulder radiograph shows distance between the the proximal aspect of the humeral head and inferior aspect of the acromion of less than 7 mm.

synonyms.val: Proximal subluxation of the humeral head

comments: Conditions characterized by this finding include rotator cuff tear arthropathy, rotator cuff tear, and shoulder external impingement syndrome.

definition.val: intracompartmental pressure (ICP) over 30 mmHg. Acute compartment syndrome occurs when there is increased pressure within a closed osteofascial compartment, resulting in impaired local circulation. Acute compartment syndrome is considered a surgical emergency since, without proper treatment, it can lead to ischemia and eventually necrosis. Generally, acute compartment syndrome is considered a clinical diagnosis. However, ICP over 30 mmHg can be used as a threshold to aid in diagnosis.

comments: Fascia is a thin, inelastic sheet of connective tissue that surrounds muscle compartments and limits the capacity for rapid expansion. The earliest objective physical finding is the tense, or wood-like feeling of the involved compartment. Pain is typically severe, out of proportion to the injury. Measurement of intracompartmental pressure is not required but can aid in diagnosis if uncertainty exists. Compartment pressures are often measured with a manometer, a device that detects intracompartmental pressure by measuring the resistance that is present when a saline solution is injected into the compartment. The normal pressure within the compartment is between 0 mmHg to 8 mmHg. An intra-compartmental pressure greater than 30 mmHg indicates compartment syndrome and a need for fasciotomy.

nodes.lbl: Pain at the lateral aspect of the elbow

definition.val: Pain localized to the radial aspect of the elbow.

nodes.lbl: Pain at the posterior aspect of the elbow

definition.val: Pain localized to the posterior aspect of the elbow.

comments: The posterior aspect of the elbow refers to the back side of the elbow, which forms the prominent bony tip of the elbow.

nodes.lbl: Pain at the medial aspect of the elbow

definition.val: Pain localized to the medial aspect of the elbow.

comments: The medial aspect of the elbow refers to the inner side of the elbow. Conditions characterized by this finding include medial epicondylitis.

definition.val: Applies to the localization of findings corresponding to the distribution of the radial nevrve, such as (i)paresthesias on the dorsoradial aspect of the hand and wrist, including the dorsal thumb, index finger and middle finger and (ii) Weakness in elbow extension, wrist extension, finger extension, thumb extension and/or supination of the forearm.
An osseous connection between the superomedial border of the right scapula and C5-C6 spinous processes.

comments: The omovertebral bone is seen in approximately one-third of patients with Sprengel deformity. The clinical presentation of SD varies, ranging from simply limited shoulder abduction and mild cosmetic deformity to severe clinical abnormalities. Nonsurgical management is appropriate for mild cases, while severe deformities require surgery. See Figure 1 of PMID:38908946.

definition.val: Swelling on the chest between the neck and the shoulder, above the clavicel (collar bone).

comments: This condition may be observed with diseases including congenital pseudoarthrosis of clavicle and clavicle shaft fracture.

definition.val: The presence of antibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that react against a component of measles virus.

synonyms.val: Elevated measles antibody titer in cerebrospinal fluid

comments: This finding may be observed with diseases including subacute sclerosing leukoencephalitis.

definition.val: Vertical lines in the posterior stroma of the cornea, aligned with Descemet membrane. These lines temporarily disappear with pressure applied to the cornea. Vogt striae are a hallmark feature of keratoconus but have also been observed in healthy eyes. Rare cases of horizontal striae have been reported.

A condition characterized by an abnormal increase in the thickness of the choroid, which may be associated with various ocular or systemic conditions. Choroid thickening can be measured using imaging techniques such as optical coherence tomography (OCT).

A condition characterized by accumulation of fluid within the corneal epithelium, leading to swelling, blurred vision, and discomfort. It is often associated with increased intraocular pressure, endothelial dysfunction, or contact lens overuse. Clinical features may include a hazy cornea and microcystic changes visible on slit-lamp examination.

comments: This finding can be observed in diseases such as Fuchs endothelial dystrophy, acute angle-closure glaucoma, and bullous keratopathy.

definition.val: bnormal blood vessels in the retina that form as a response to vascular occlusion, serving as bypass channels to redirect blood flow around obstructed or damaged retinal vessels. Retinal shunt vessels are often associated with conditions like retinal vein occlusion or diabetic retinopathy and may appear as tortuous or dilated vessels on fundoscopic examination.

comments: See Figure 12 of PMID:37238303.

definition.val: A condition characterized by the formation of filaments composed of degenerated epithelial cells and mucus attached to the corneal surface. It is associated with symptoms such as pain, foreign body sensation, photophobia, and tearing. Filamentary keratitis is often linked to underlying conditions such as dry eye disease, post-surgical ocular surface disorders, or systemic diseases like Sjoegren syndrome.
Concentration of D-glucosylsphingosine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

comments: Glucosylsphingosine (GlcSph) is a key biomarker of Gaucher Disease.

definition.val: A condition characterized by bleeding at or near the optic disc, visible as a flame-shaped or splinter hemorrhage on fundoscopic examination.

comments: Optic disc bleeding is a significant clinical marker in glaucoma, particularly normal-tension glaucoma, and is associated with disease progression. It may result from mechanical stress on the lamina cribrosa or vascular dysregulation.

definition.val: The concentration of progranulin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

comments: Progranulin, a secreted glycoprotein, maintains cerebrocortical viability. It has been identified as an important factor controlling neural function while also suppressing neuroinflammation and playing roles in neuronal lysosome function. Loss of one allele of GRN, the gene encoding progranulin, leads to the development of frontotemporal dementia, and loss of both alleles leads to the development of neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis.

definition.val: Enlargement of one or more lymph nodes located in front of the ear.
Growth of nail tissue outside the ungual plate, generally in the finger.

A deviation from the normal level of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules expressed at the cell surface. The cell-mediated adaptive immune response is regulated by the MHC, which is called human leukocyte antigen (HLA) in humans. HLA molecules are cell surface glycoproteins whose primary function is to present endogenous and exogenous antigens to T lymphocytes for recognition and response. The HLA molecules that present antigen to T lymphocytes are divided into two main classes: HLA class I and HLA class II molecules.

nodes.lbl: Forward displacement of posterior cervical dura mater on neck flexion

definition.val: Flexion MRI (imaging with neutral and flexed about 30-40 degrees neck position) reveals an anterior shift of the cervical dural sac from the lamina in the region of C4 to C7.

comments: This finding is characteristic of Monomelic amyotrophy (Hirayama disease) is a rare motor neuron disorder characterized by progressive weakness and atrophy in the distal upper extremities, typically beginning during adolescence. The condition involves asymmetric muscle atrophy in the hand and forearm, sparing the brachioradialis muscle, and is attributed to increased laxity in the dura mater, which causes the spinal cord to shift forward during neck flexion. Increased laxity of the dura mater from its superior anchors on the dorsal surfaces of C2 and C3, harbingering forward cord movement during cervical flexion. Increased laxity allows the spinal cord to shift forward, leading to repeated subclinical trauma and microischemia in the anterior horn during cervical flexion. Trauma and microischemia eventually lead to myelopathy and degeneration, as evidenced by asymmetric lower cervical cord thinning within the C7 and C8.

definition.val: A localized area of corneal thinning typically occurring adjacent to an elevated lesion, such as a conjunctival scar, pterygium, or poorly fitting contact lens. Corneal dellen result from tear film instability and localized dehydration. Without timely treatment, they may progress to epithelial defects or corneal ulceration.

comments: Diseases characterized by this finding include corneal pterygium, corneal ulceration, and post-surgical ocular surface disorder.

definition.val: A condition characterized by dryness of the conjunctiva, often associated with keratinization of the conjunctival epithelium. Conjunctival xerosis is commonly linked to vitamin A deficiency, severe dry eye disease, or systemic conditions such as Sjogren syndrome. Clinical features may include a dull, rough conjunctival surface and reduced mucosal secretions.

comments: Diseases characterized by this term include vitamin A deficiency, Sjogren syndrome, and Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

definition.val: Difficulty rotating the lower part of the arm away from the body (tested with the elbow flexed and the elbow held next to the side of the body) secondary to pain, weakness, or mechanical block.

comments: Diseases characterized by this finding include rotator cuff tear.

nodes.lbl: Occupational exposure to frequent hand trauma

definition.val: A history of exposure to repeated hand trauma as observed with occupations in which use of hands is frequent such as construction, food preparation and serving related occupations, and transportation and material moving occupations.

nodes.lbl: Inability to fully extend finger at metacarpophalangeal joint

definition.val: An inability to fully extend the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint of a finger (extension of an MCP joint straightens the finger).

synonyms.val: Inability to fully extend finger at MCP joint
Inability to fully extend finger from base

definition.val: Inflammation of the wrist joint.

comments: Symptoms of arthritis include pain, swelling, redness, stiffness, and loss of motion of the involved joint. Three primary types of arthritis affect the human wrist: osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and post-traumatic arthritis.

definition.val: Widening of the space between the scaphoid and lunate on x-ray; scapholunate dissociation.

Applies to an abnormality whose distribution is limited to or predominantly affects the fleshy mass on the volar (palmar) aspect of the digit, distal to the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint (known as the pulp of the finger).

synonyms.val: Symptoms localized to pulp of the finger

definition.val: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the ulnar side of the wrist.

comments: The ulnar side of the wrist is the side of the wrist closest to the little finger (fifth finger, pinky). Conditions characterized by this term include triangular fibrocartilage complex, distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ) arthritis, and pisotriquetral (PT) osteoarthritis.

definition.val: Radiographic widening of the space between the lunate and triquetrum bones.

comments: This finding may be observed with lunotriquetral ligament injury.

definition.val: Anteroposterior wrist radiograph showing ulnar translocation of the carpus from the distal radius with widening of the radial styloid-scaphoid space.

comments: This finding may be observed with Carpal instability nondissociative (CIND).

nodes.lbl: Snapping sensation at time of injury

definition.val: A popping or snapping sensation (noise or feeling) at the time of an injury.

comments: Sudden snapping or popping at the time of an injury can be a sign of significant damage to muscles, tendons, ligaments, or bones.

definition.val: Pagetoid spread connotes the spread of single neoplastic cells, and small nests of them above the basal layer in a variety of melanocytic and nonmelanocytic neoplasms similar to the pattern seen in Paget's and in extramammary Paget disease.

comments: Pagetoid proliferation of single melanocytic cells or small nests of melanocytes may be seen in a variety of melanocytic neoplasms including pagetoid spitz nevi, de novo epithelioid melanocytic dysplasia, and melanoma. Pagetoid melanocytosis may also be a common feature of acral nevi, traumatized nevi, or in nevi after acute sun exposure.

definition.val: Central scarring of skin lesions.

A breakage (partial or complete tear) of the scapholunate ligament. The most common cause is physical trauma to the wrist such as a fall onto an outstretched hand. Tear of the scapholunate ligament may lead to carpal instability.

comments: Together with the lunotriquetral interosseous ligament, the scapholunate ligament is one of the two proximal interosseous carpal ligaments of the wrist. It is a C-shaped ligament that binds the scaphoid bone to the lunate bone of the wrist. A scapholunate tear can be partial or complete. Since it is C-shaped, it often is only one limb of the C that is torn.

definition.val: A breakage (partial or complete tear) of the lunotriquetral ligament. The most common cause is physical trauma to the wrist such as a fall onto an outstretched hand. Rupture or tear of the the lunotriquetral ligament may lead to carpal instability.

comments: The scapholunate and lunotriquetral interosseous ligaments form the interconnections between the bones of the proximal carpal row and share several anatomic features. Each forms a barrier between the radiocarpal and midcarpal joints, connecting the dorsal, proximal, and palmar edges of the respective joint surfaces.

definition.val: Arthritis at the pisotriquetral joint. Radiographic evidence of arthritis at the pisotriquetral joint includes joint space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral cysts, and/or subchondral sclerosis.
A type of carpal instability characterized by volar tilt of the lunate bone.

comments: Lateral wrist radiograph showing volar flexion of the lunate with a scapholunate angle less than 30 degrees. This finding may be observed with conditions such as lunotriquetral ligament injury and carpal instability nondissociative.

nodes.lbl: Inaccurate finger pulse oximetry oxygen saturation measurement

definition.val: Any substantial discrepancy between the measurement of oxygen saturation with finger probe pulse oximetry as compared to an arterial blood gas, which is considered the gold standard.

comments: Pulse oximetry is an useful, readily available and non-invasive tool of measuring oxygen saturation. It uses light sensors containing two light sources of different wavelengths, that are absorbed by haemoglobin (both oxy and deoxy forms) and transmitted through tissues to a photodetector. Any discrepancy in the light transmission caused either by vascular abnormality of the fingers or anatomical change may lead to inaccurate or absence of reading in the pulse oximeter.

nodes.lbl: Finger pulse oximetry lower than arterial blood gas analysis measurement of oxygen saturation

definition.val: Inaccurately reduced oxygen saturation as measured by finger or toe pulse oximetry compared to oxygen saturation as measured by venous or arterial blood gas analysis.

comments: This feature may be observed with conditions such as Raynaud phenomenon and scleroderma, in which peripheral microvasculopathy leads to poor perfusion of the fingers.

nodes.lbl: Finger pulse oximetry higher than arterial blood gas analysis measurement of oxygen saturation

definition.val: Inaccurately elevated oxygen saturation as measured by finger or toe pulse oximetry compared to oxygen saturation as measured by venous or arterial blood gas analysis.

comments: This feature may be observed with Carbon monoxide poisoning. Presently available pulse oximeters overestimate arterial oxygenation in patients with severe CO poisoning. An elevated COHb level falsely elevates the SaO2 measurements from pulse oximetry.

nodes.lbl: History of thumb sucking past the age of four years

definition.val: Thumb sucking is a behavior that ceases spontaneously in most children between 2 and 4 years of age. If thumb sucking continues, negative consequences can occur, such as a deformity of the nail or paronychia. This term refers to a history of habitual thumb sucking past the age of 4 years of life.

Skin inflammatory reaction triggered by a wide variety of stimuli, including infections, foreign bodies, malignancy, metabolites, and chemicals. From a pathogenic point of view, they are divided into non-infectious and infectious granulomas. From a clinical point of view, it is useful to divide cutaneous granulomatosis into localized and more disseminated forms, although this distinction can be sometimes artificial.
Obstruction of urine flow through one or both ureters caused by issues such as injury, infection, tumours and surgery.

A retinal vascular abnormality characterized by indentation or compression of a retinal vein at an arteriovenous crossing, leading to changes in venous caliber. AV crossing signs are commonly associated with hypertensive retinopathy and may contribute to retinal vein occlusion. They are indicative of vascular remodeling due to chronic hypertension or other systemic vascular diseases.

comments: This feature may be present in diseases such as hypertensive retinopathy and retinal vein occlusion.

definition.val: Curvilinear or circumferential breaks in Descemet membrane, typically associated with congenital glaucoma. Haab striae result from elevated intraocular pressure during corneal development, leading to the formation of horizontal or arcuate lines that may be visible on slit-lamp examination. They can contribute to corneal astigmatism and visual impairment.
Growth of Legionella bacteria in a sputum culture.
Streptococcus pneumoniae growth in sputum culture.

nodes.lbl: Positive Blastomyces dermatitidis sputum fungal stain

definition.val: Demonstration of Blastomyces dermatitidis by microscopic examination of a stained sputum specimen.

synonyms.val: Blastomyces dermatitidis on sputum fungal stain

comments: Blastomycosis is a fungal infection caused by Blastomyces dermatitidis. It presents as a pulmonary infection after the inhalation of spores, and it may be either asymptomatic or have severe life-threatening complications like acute respiratory distress syndrome.

definition.val: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the posterior (back) part of the shoulder.

comments: Posterior shoulder pain may be observed in conditions such as shoulder internal impingement syndrome, suprascapular neuropathy, labrum tear, and shoulder dislocation.

definition.val: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the superior or proximal aspect of the shoulder over the acromion, distal clavicle, and/or acromioclavicular (AC) joint.

comments: Superior shoulder pain may be observed in conditions such as acromioclavicular joint injury, acromioclavicular joint osteoarthritis, and distal clavicle osteolysis.

definition.val: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the localized aspect (on the side) of the shoulder.

comments: Lateral shoulder pain may be observed in conditions such as proximal humerus fracture, proximal humeral epiphysiolysis, adhesive capsulitis, and suprascapular neuropathy.

definition.val: Subjective or objective feeling of clunking/clicking in the shoulder with movement, shoulder 'giving way', or sensation of shoulder dislocating.

comments: Shoulder instability may be observed in conditions such as shoulder dislocation, labrum tear, and suprascapular neuropathy.

definition.val: A injury with a team (rip, split, or disruption) to the labrum, which is the ring of cartilage that surrounds the socket of the shoulder joint (the glenoid).

comments: Shoulder labral tears can be classified as superior Labral Anterior Posterior tear (SLAP); bankart lesion; anterior labral periosteal sleeve avulsion (ALPSA); and glenoid labral articular defect (GLAD) and may be observed in conditions such as shoulder dislocation, shoulder internal impingement syndrome, and acromioclavicular joint injury.

nodes.lbl: Positive modified dynamic labral shear test

definition.val: Sensation of a pain with or without clicking or clunking sensation with the following test. Flex patients elbow to 90 degrees and abduct the arm 120 degrees while maximally externally rotating the arm, then examiner lowers the arm to 60 degrees of abduction. A positive test occurs with pain and/or a painful click along the posterior joint line between 120 degrees and 90 degrees of abduction.

comments: This test is frequently positive with labrum tear of the shoulder.

definition.val: Pain in shoulder reproduced when examiner applies downward pressure on the arm while patient resists pressure in the following position: elbow extended, shoulder forward flexed to 90 degrees and 10-15 degrees adducted with palm facing down. This can be compared to the same position but with the palm facing up which should be less painful.

comments: A positive test may be observed in conditions such as acromioclavicular joint injury, shoulder labrum tear, adhesive capsulitis, and biceps subluxation.

definition.val: The individual being investigated displays noticeable apprehension (unease) during a test for shoulder instability in which the individual is laying supine with shoulder abducted to 90 degrees, elbow flexed to 90 degrees, and an external rotation pressure with combined downward pressure is applied on the upper arm.
A condition characterized by the presence of foam or bubbles within the tear film, often associated with meibomian gland dysfunction or ocular surface diseases.

comments: This feature may be observed in conditions such as Meibomian gland dysfunction and blepharitis.

definition.val: The formation of large, bluish, nodular lesions in the superficial corneal stroma, often associated with chronic keratitis or aging. These nodules may lead to visual impairment.

The abnormal growth of blood vessels into the corneal stroma, often associated with ocular herpes, chronic inflammation, infection, or hypoxia. This condition can lead to corneal scarring and vision impairment.

comments: This feature may be observed in herpetic eye disease.

definition.val: Linear or arcuate deposition of iron within the corneal epithelium or stroma, typically associated with conditions such as keratoconus, corneal degeneration, or postsurgical corneal changes.
A condition characterized by redundant, loose conjunctival tissue, typically located between the globe and the lower eyelid, which may cause ocular discomfort, tear film instability, or epiphora.

comments: Conjunctivochalasis can be observed with conditions such as dry eye and floppy eyelid syndrome.

definition.val: Increased pigmentation of the conjunctiva, characterized by brown or black discoloration due to melanocytic proliferation or pigment deposition. It may be associated with benign conditions such as primary acquired melanosis or malignant transformation into conjunctival melanoma.
Antibodies against antigens presented by the cell wall of the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

comments: Anti-Saccharomyces cerevisiae antibodies (ASCAs) have been used as a marker for Crohn disease, Behcet disease, celiac disease, and other conditions.

definition.val: The fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) is elevated above the upper limit of normal. FeNO is an endogenous gaseous molecule which can be measured in the human breath test because of airway inflammation. It has been studied extensively as a marker of inflammation and has been incorporated into an algorithm for asthma management.

comments: Fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) is a simple, reproducible, and a noninvasive marker of inflammation that may be elevated in diseases such as ssthma, eosinophilic pneumonia, COPD, pulmonary fibrosis, and interstitial lung disease.

definition.val: A condition characterized by increased blood flow and congestion of the iris vasculature, leading to a reddish discoloration of the iris. Iris hyperemia is commonly associated with anterior uveitis, angle-closure glaucoma, or ocular inflammation.
The number of reticulated platelets per volume of blood in the peripheral circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

comments: Reticulated platelets (RPs) are young, hyper-reactive platelets that are newly released from the bone marrow. RPs are thus immature platelets circulating in blood; they reflect the activity of megakaryopoiesis in the bone marrow.They are larger and contain more RNA compared to older platelets. In comparison to more mature platelets, they exhibit a significantly higher thrombogenicity and are known to be elevated in patients with an increased platelet turnover such as, diabetics and after acute myocardial infarction.

definition.val: The number of reticulated platelets per volume of blood in the peripheral circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

comments: Reticulated platelets (RPs) are young, hyper-reactive platelets that are newly released from the bone marrow. RPs are thus immature platelets circulating in blood; they reflect the activity of megakaryopoiesis in the bone marrow.They are larger and contain more RNA compared to older platelets. In comparison to more mature platelets, they exhibit a significantly higher thrombogenicity and are known to be elevated in patients with an increased platelet turnover such as, diabetics and after acute myocardial infarction.

definition.val: The number of reticulated platelets per volume of blood in the peripheral circulation is outside the limits of normal.

comments: Reticulated platelets (RPs) are young, hyper-reactive platelets that are newly released from the bone marrow. RPs are thus immature platelets circulating in blood; they reflect the activity of megakaryopoiesis in the bone marrow.They are larger and contain more RNA compared to older platelets. In comparison to more mature platelets, they exhibit a significantly higher thrombogenicity and are known to be elevated in patients with an increased platelet turnover such as, diabetics and after acute myocardial infarction.

definition.val: A sign that can be observed in diseases such as Pyogenic or suppurative flexor tenosynovitis in which the affected finger is held in a flexed position. Often, there is pain on any attempt at passive finger extension. This finding is to be distinguished from a contracture of a finger joint in which the flexed positions is fixed.

comments: This finding is one of the four Kanavel signs for pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis: (i) flexed posturing of the involved digit; (ii) tenderness to palpation over the tendon sheath; (iii) marked pain with passive extension of the digit; and (iv) fusiform swelling of the digit.

definition.val: Elevation of the the alpha-defensin concentration in synovial aspirate is above the upper limit of normal. The alpha-defensin test is a qualitative immunoassay optimized and validated for synovial fluid. The alpha-defensin protein is an antimicrobial peptide that is naturally released by neutrophils responding to a pathogen in the synovial fluid.

comments: The alpha-defensin test has been previously demonstrated to be highly accurate in the diagnosis of prosthetic joint infection.

definition.val: Salter-Harris fractures (physeal fractures) refer to fractures through a growth plate (physis) and are, therefore, specifically applied to bone fractures in children.

A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture line extends through the physis or within the growth plate. Type I fractures are due to the longitudinal force applied through the physis, which splits the epiphysis from the metaphysis.

comments: Beware that a normal radiograph cannot exclude a physis injury in a symptomatic pediatric patient. A radiograph may be normal due to lack of bony involvement, and mild to moderate soft tissue swelling may be noted. Look for the widening of the physis or displacement of the epiphysis, which may suggest a fracture. Diagnosis is based on clinical findings, such as the presence of focal tenderness or swelling surrounding the growth plate.

definition.val: A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture extends through both the physis and metaphysis. These are most common and occur away from the joint space. When the small corner of the metaphysis is visible, this is known as a corner sign or Thurston-Holland fragment.
A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture is intra-articular and extends from the physis into the epiphysis.

comments: If the fracture extends the complete length of the physis, this type of fracture may form two epiphyseal segments. Since the epiphysis is involved, damage to the articular cartilage may occur. One example is a Tillaux fracture of the ankle, which is a fracture of the anterolateral aspect of the growth plate and epiphysis.

definition.val: A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture is intra-articular and passes through the epiphysis, physis, and metaphysis.

comments: As this fracture involves the epiphysis, the articular cartilage may be damaged. Types III and IV fractures each carry a risk for growth retardation, altered joint mechanics, and functional impairment. Therefore, both require urgent orthopedic evaluation.

definition.val: A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture that is due to a crush or compression injury of the growth plate. In type V, the force is transmitted through the epiphysis and physis, potentially disrupting the germinal matrix, hypertrophic region, and vascular supply.

comments: Though Harris-Salter V fractures are very rare, they may be seen in electric shock, frostbite, and irradiation cases. As this fracture pattern tends to result from severe injury, these typically have a poor prognosis leading to bone growth arrest.

definition.val: A cut or injury to the soft tissue under the fingernail or toenail.
Recent or remote history of distal radius fracture of the symptomatic arm.

comments: This finding refers to a medical history of distal radius fracture in the arm that is the focus of current medical attention. This finding may relate to scapholunate advanced collapse, distal radioulnar joint arthritis, and scapholunate ligament injury.

nodes.lbl: History of triangular fibrocartilage complex tear

definition.val: Recent or remote history of a tear in the triangular fibrocartilage complex (TFCC). The TFCC is a load-bearing structure between the lunate, triquetrum, and ulnar head. The function of the TFCC is to act as a stabilizer for the ulnar aspect of the wrist. The TFCC is at risk for either acute or chronic degenerative injury.

comments: Such a history is important for the diagnosis of Distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ) arthritis.

definition.val: The creases (wrinkles) on the soles of the feet are less pronounced than normal, or absent.

comments: This finding may be seen in premature infants and in some conditions such as GFRA1-related Apert syndrome, renal hypodysplasia/aplasia 4, and Atelis syndrome 2.

definition.val: Damage to the skin and underlying tissues caused by an agents such as heat, chemicals, electricity, radiation, or friction, resulting in pain, redness, swelling, and sometimes blisters or charring.

comments: This term does not refer to sunburn.

nodes.lbl: Elevanted carboxysterol concentration in cultured lymphoblasts

definition.val: The concentration of carboxysterols in lymphoblastoid cells cultured in cholesterol-depleted medium is below the lower limit of normal.

comments: When cultured in cholesterol-depleted medium, lymphoblastoid cells of individuals with CHILD syndrome and CK syndrome have increased levels of methyl- and carboxysterols and slightly decreased levels of cholesterol.

definition.val: An anomaly that can be ascertained by iron-specific magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequences such as gradient-echo (GRE) and susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI). Superficial siderosis of the central nervous system is a chronic condition due to persistent or repeated long-term bleeding into the subarachnoid space, leading to subpial hemosiderin deposition. Hemosiderin deposition on MRI is seen as a T2 hypointensity and preferentially outlines the cerebellum and brainstem surface.

comments: Superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition is a manifestation of superficial siderosis (SS) of the central nervous system (CNS), which is typically due to chronic low-grade extravasation of blood into the subarachnoid space. Hemoglobin in red blood cells in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) breaks down into globin and neurotoxic heme. In response to the presence of neurotoxic heme, neuroglial cells release hemoxygenase and apoferritin. Hemoxygenase breaks heme into free iron and biliverdin, and apoferritin binds free iron to form ferritin and subsequently hemosiderin. This process is likely neuroprotective and prevents free iron mediated neuronal injury. Persistence of blood in the subarachnoid space eventually overwhelms the ferritin production capacity and unbound iron results in free-radical mediated neuronal injury. Hemosiderin deposits in regions of the brain or spinal cord adjacent to CSF. This confluent subpial hemosiderin deposition results in a characteristic marginal and confluent T2-hypointensity on magnetic resonance imaging that is referred to as SS and it is best appreciated on iron-sensitive sequences.

definition.val: A type of superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition that most commonly occurs due to iron deposits in the superficial cortical layers following bleeding from leptomeningeal vessels, most often from cerebral amyloid angiopathy in patients aged 55 or older.

A type of superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition that involves the cerebellum and brainstem, most commonly the superior vermis, quadrigeminal plate, and basal cerebral surfaces. Cerebellar atrophy, particularly the superior vermis and anterior cerebellar hemispheres, can also be seen on a computed tomography scan of the head. The MRI of the spinal cord may reveal myelomalacia, syringomyelia, owl-eyes, or snake-eyes signs. The most common etiology for classic or primary infratentorial superficial siderosis is spinal dural defects, often dural tears.

Pulmonary Hyperplasia is an absolute increase in the number of alveoli, which are mildly enlarged. Pulmonary hyperplasia has been also referred to as polyalveolar lobe and type 3 cystic adenomatoid malformation.

comments: The pathogenesis and clinical characteristics of pulmonary hyperplasia are related to congenital lobar overinflation/emphysema, but should be distinguished. In the latter condition, the volume increase is due to alveolar enlargement as opposed to an absolute increase in alveoli. Radial alveolar counts can be helpful for distinguishing between these two abnormalities. Pulmonary hyperplasia may be associated with in utero death due to compression of venous return to the heart and/or esophageal compression, resulting in polyhydramnios and fetal hydrops. The therapy for infants with lobar distension causing severe mediastinal shift and normal lung compression is surgical removal of the affected lobe or segment.

nodes.lbl: Positive protozoan parasite CSF wet mount test

definition.val: Demonstration of protozoan parasites in a cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) specimen by microscopy.

A gallbladder (GB) polyp is a growth that projects from the lining of the inside wall of the gallbladder into the lumen of the GB. GB polyps are a common incidental sonographic finding, the vast majority of which are benign.

comments: Most benign GB polyps are non-neoplastic, including cholesterol pseudopolyps and inflammatory polyps.

definition.val: Multiple polyps arising from the gallbladder mucosal wall.
Discontinuity of the biceps tendon as observed by ultrasound or magnetic resonance (MR) imaging.

comments: Patients suffering from biceps tendon rupture may complain of sudden sharp pain in the elbow or shoulder, depending on the site of the rupture. Usually, there is a history of sudden eccentric force to a flexed elbow. They may feel an audible pop in the affected arm at the time of the injury. Pain can persist for weeks to months.

definition.val: Medial epicondyle apophysitis (MEA), also known as little league elbow, is an overuse injury prevalent among adolescent athletes whose sport involves repetitive overhand throwing, racket use, or other overhead arm motions. The medial epicondyle is a bony protrusion on the medial elbow with its own ossification center, separate from the main distal humeral physis, known as an apophysis. Medial epicondyle apophysitis occurs due to excessive and repetitive valgus stress placed on the apophysis before its closure. Over time, the repetitive strain results in a traction-type injury and may cause pathologic widening and inflammation of the apophysis or even an avulsion fracture.

A partial (subluxation) loss of alignment at the base of the thumb, where the first metacarpal bone meets the trapezium bone of the wrist. Thumb radiographs showing carpometacarpal (CMC) joint space widening and/or incongruity of the joint space between thumb metacarpal bone and the trapezium bone.

A descriptor indicating that a condition, lesion, or abnormality is confined to the lower eyelid. This localization may be relevant for various ocular conditions, including infections, structural abnormalities, or dermatological diseases affecting the lower eyelid region.

comments: An anatomical spatial pattern or localization referring to the lower eyelid, the smaller, less mobile fold of skin and tissue positioned below the eye.

definition.val: Applies to an abnormality that is situated in an eyelid.

A visual phenomenon characterized by the perception of bright rings or halos surrounding light sources. Halo vision is often associated with optical irregularities such as corneal edema, cataracts, or intraocular lens complications. It may also occur in conditions affecting the tear film or due to the presence of glare from light scattering within the ocular media.
The presence of blood in the seminal fluid.
Choledocholithiasis is the presence of stones within the common bile duct.

comments: It is estimated that common bile duct stones are present in anywhere from 1-15% of patients with cholelithiasis.

definition.val: Paresthesias on the lateral aspect of the shoulder and upper arm. Weakness in shoulder abduction (deltoid) and shoulder external rotation (teres minor).

X-ray of the pelvis (AP, inlet, and outlet views) showing fracture of the pelvic ring, including iliac wing (ilium), superior or inferior pubic ramus, or ischium, and/or displacement of the pubic symphysis or sacroiliac joints.

An injury consisting of a laterally displaced scapula with separation of the ipsilateral acromioclavicular joint, disruption of the ipsilateral subclavian vessels and brachial plexus, and an intact overlying skin.

comments: Scapulothoracic dissociation may be associated with a laterally displaced scapula with an ipsilateral distracted clavicular fracture (most common type), acromioclavicular joint separation or less commonly sternoclavicular joint disruption, without or with concomitant injuries to the ipsilateral subclavian or axillary vessels and the brachial plexus.

definition.val: Refers to pain that is worse when the individual bears weight with the affected body part.

comments: This feature may be observed in conditions such as hip fracture, tibial shaft fracture, calcaneus fracture, and ankle sprain.

definition.val: The distal phalanx of the adducted thumb extends beyond the ulnar border of the palm (The thumb protrudes from the clenched fist).

comments: The Steinberg or the thumb sign is elicited by asking the patient to fold his thumb into the closed fist. If the thumb tip extends from the palm of the hand, the test is positive.

definition.val: Partial or complete breakage (rupture) of the tibialis anterior tendon (TAT). The TAT is the principal dorsiflexor of the ankle joint and secondary invertor of the foot.
